raw_text:
Supported signature algorithms should be determined by Cert Verifier

1. The ServerCertVerifier and ClientCertVerifier interfaces should be extended to allow them to filter which signature schemes (algorithms, digest algorithms, and curves) are supported. This would be analogous to what's possible with `ResolvesClientCert`/`ResolvesServerCert`/`Signer`.

2. The provided implementations like `AllowAnyAnonymousOrAuthenticatedClient` should allow the user to provide a filter for signature schemes so that one doesn't have to implement a custom "dangerous" implementation of the traits.

3. Everywhere that the client/server advertises supported signature algorithms & curves, it should filter the list using the `ServerCertVerifier`/`ClientCertVerifier`.

Example use case: An application may only want to trust one kind of signature scheme (e.g. ECDSA) in order to minimize the amount of crypto code it relies on.

Impl<T> From<T> for Stream<T> where T: Read

# Feature Request

`Stream` currently has a method called from that takes a `Read` object and returns a Stream. It would be nice if `Stream` implemented `From` so that we could call `.into()` on our `Read` types.

This would be useful in reducing the amount of code written for returning a `Stream` object. Currently in order to return a `Stream` one must type `Stream::from(reader)`, if this impl was added you could simply write `reader.into()`.

This feature needs to exist in Rocket since the Stream type is defined there and impls of traits for types must be done in the same crate.

raw_text:
Include the URL that could not be requested in `reqwest::Error`

There is no programmatic way to know which URL failed when making a request. The URL given to `RequestBuilder` is not necessarily the one that failed because of redirects, and even if `RequestBuilder` did expose ithe URL it was created with (it doesn't have a getter for it at the moment) it gets consumed by `send()` anyway. So it seems to me the `Error` returned by `send()` would be the correct place to include this URL.

It would be even better to include a `Vec` of URLs in case of redirects.

RequestBuilder headers() method behaviour different than header() with multiple values for same key

When adding headers through headers() one at a time all keys are properly set. However when constructing a HeaderMap beforehand and adding it using headers(), only one value from a certain key is kept.

Is this the desired behaviour? It surprised me and took a while to debug until I echoed the full request that was actually sent.

Caused by using insert() in headers() and append() in header().

https://github.com/seanmonstar/reqwest/blob/c4985674aaa1cd23ec70ee7dfc24c76b714285c5/src/request.rs#L192

https://github.com/seanmonstar/reqwest/blob/c4985674aaa1cd23ec70ee7dfc24c76b714285c5/src/request.rs#L151


EDIT: Apparently even when I append manually, they are removed when sending. Seems like its impossible to send multiple headers.

https://github.com/seanmonstar/reqwest/blob/c4985674aaa1cd23ec70ee7dfc24c76b714285c5/src/async_impl/client.rs#L452


These examples are then broken because they would never be sent:
https://docs.rs/reqwest/0.9.5/reqwest/header/struct.HeaderMap.html#method.append

In that example, only "earth" is actually sent in the network request.

`GET / HTTP/1.1
user-agent: reqwest/0.9.5
accept: */*
host: earth
accept-encoding: gzip`

raw_text:
"System" proxies should be used by default

Hi,
currently proxies need to be manually added using a client builder. I strongly disagree with https://github.com/seanmonstar/reqwest/issues/30#issuecomment-271714181 that reqwest should not handle the system proxies automatically. I think it should use them by default, and for the rare where proxies should not be used, a builder can be used to disable them.

Think of the thousands of command line utilities that do http requests that were only tested in environnements that work without proxies (my last example being https://github.com/gobanos/cargo-aoc/blob/54e0a80a9bd7dc339c7d2c9dbbf43076d9112e3a/src/app.rs#L66 ). Do they all need to add code to explicitly say they want to use the user's configured proxy ?

As mentionned in https://github.com/seanmonstar/reqwest/issues/30#issuecomment-266336609 the crate env_proxy https://crates.io/crates/env_proxy can be used for basic support.

Ideally, more system methods would be recognized (java has support for the windows registry and for gnome gconf : see https://github.com/openjdk-mirror/jdk7u-jdk/blob/f4d80957e89a19a29bb9f9807d2a28351ed7f7df/src/windows/native/sun/net/spi/DefaultProxySelector.c  and https://github.com/openjdk-mirror/jdk7u-jdk/blob/f4d80957e89a19a29bb9f9807d2a28351ed7f7df/src/solaris/native/sun/net/spi/DefaultProxySelector.c )

Cheers,
Jon

Datetime fields are not serialized by .into_json() on queries

## Description
When using the `.into_json()` method to load the result of a query into a `JsonValue` object, the resulting JSON is missing any date/datetime fields (chrono `Date`/`DateTime<Tz>` objects) that were present in the model. 

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a model/database with date and/or datetime fields.
2. Query the data in that model.
3. Call `.into_json()` on the result.

### Expected Behavior

The JsonValue object will include String representations of datetimes in YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (or similar) format, as is the result of serializing the model with `serde_json::json!()`.

### Actual Behavior
The resulting JsonValue has the correct structure, but any date or datetime fields are missing.

### Reproduces How Often

Every time.

## Versions

├── sea-orm v0.6.0
│   ├── sea-orm-macros v0.6.0 (proc-macro)
│   ├── sea-query v0.21.0
│   │   ├── sea-query-derive v0.2.0 (proc-macro)
│   ├── sea-strum v0.23.0
│   │   └── sea-strum_macros v0.23.0 (proc-macro)

│   ├── sqlx v0.5.10
│   │   ├── sqlx-core v0.5.10
│   │   │   ├── sqlformat v0.1.8
│   │   │   ├── sqlx-rt v0.5.10
│   │   └── sqlx-macros v0.5.10 (proc-macro)
│   │       ├── sqlx-core v0.5.10 (\*)
│   │       ├── sqlx-rt v0.5.10 (\*)

I'm using MySQL 8.0 on Windows 10. 

## Additional Information

Relevant lines from Cargo.toml (remaining crates are actix dependencies and other unrelated items):

    chrono = { version = "^0.4", features = ["serde"] }
    serde = "^1.0"
    serde_json = "^1.0"

    [dependencies.sea-orm]
    version = "^0.6.0"
    default-features = false
    features = ["macros", "runtime-actix-native-tls", "debug-print", "with-json", "with-chrono"]

    [features]
    default = ["sqlx-mysql"]
    sqlx-mysql = ["sea-orm/sqlx-mysql"]

[Here is a minimal repository showing the issue.](https://github.com/e-rhodes/sea_orm_json_datetime_example)

axum-core 0.2.8 doesn't have a changelog mentioning new DefaultBodyLimit

## Overview

There is a new version of axum-core (0.2.8) on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/axum-core), which introduces quite a large change (a default request body size - see [DefaultBodyLimit](https://docs.rs/axum-core/0.2.8/axum_core/extract/struct.DefaultBodyLimit.html)) - but this isn't captured [in the axum-core changelog](https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum/blob/main/axum-core/CHANGELOG.md).

After an overlooked lock-file update on our end, we've been starting to get new errors on our servers due to this new limit, and searching for Axum `LengthLimitError` didn't really seem to help.

So I just wanted to raise this issue to (A) flag the missing change-log entry, and also to (B) help future googlers.

The full error, when using the `Json` extractor on a payload larger than 2MB was:
```
BytesRejection(FailedToBufferBody(LengthLimitError(LengthLimitError(Error { inner: LengthLimitError }))))
```

Many layers are *very* simple, and it'd be useful to have a way to create one from a closure.

### Example implementation

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct LayerFn<F>(F);

impl<F, S, Out> Layer<S> for LayerFn<F>
where
    F: Fn(S) -> Out,
{
    type Service = Out;

    fn layer(&self, inner: S) -> Self::Service {
        (self.0)(inner)
    }
}
```

Suggestion: Document Steer + Reconnect combo

Hi there,

I have a doc suggestion.

# Background

Steer provides functionality to aid managing routing requests between Services.

Current `Steer::poll_ready` implementation polls all inner services beforehand:

https://github.com/tower-rs/tower/blob/7f004da56fa3b18d60f1ee7abe6a209ed6c48488/tower/src/steer/mod.rs#L139-L153

There has been some discussion about trade-offs and alternative strategies already:

> And for the interested reader: the reason we **need to poll all services** is that we do not know at the time of the `poll_ready` which service the request subsequently sent to `call` will be for. We have two options. Either, we unconditionally accept the next element, and only then `poll_ready` on the relevant service, but then we are forced to buffer potentially an unlimited number of elements in case they are all for an unready service. Or, we get head-of-line blocking because _every_ request requires _all_ services to be ready. I suppose _in theory_ there is a third option of trying to "guess" which service the next request will be for, but that still deteriorates to the "buffer indefinitely" in the worst case.

_Originally posted by @jonhoo in https://github.com/tower-rs/tower/issues/426#issuecomment-597267568_

With that said, I would like to add an extra "gotcha" that this implementation has. If one inner services fails to poll_ready, the Steer must be dropped, and all inner services must be recreated, which could be expensive and complex. Steer is this service that becomes more valuable the more services it routes. Unfortunately, more services also means higher chances for poll_ready to fail, and more expensive and complex drop/recover becomes, kind of cancelling out its motivation.

# My suggestion

I think one way around this could be `Steer<Reconnect<MakeService<BoxService>>>`. The idea being that `MakeService::poll_ready` "most likely" has a smaller chance to fail. I think documenting this idea and the reasoning can be helpful for users considering Steer.

Today's doc suggests `Steer<BoxService>`, which works, but could be expensive depending on how many inner services you have and how fragile these are.

cheers

[Feature Request] `TimeoutLayer` supports per-request values

Right now, `TimeoutLayer` accepts a `Duration` parameter which specifies how long to wait before aborting a response. I'd like to customize this parameter on a per-request basis.

I'm envisioning this should be doable with a trait with one method; that method takes in a request and returns the `Duration`. We should be able to implement this trait for `Duration` itself so this won't be a breaking change.

raw_text:
Lack of downcast support for web-sys

For example, when I get an `Element` from some interface, and I'm sure it is a `HTMLInputElement` and I need to use its specific property, there is no way to do so. Currently I can do `unsafe { transmute::<_, HTMLInputElement>(elem) }`, but it's ugly and uses [the least safe function](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nomicon/transmutes.html) in Rust.

It would be better if there is some trait to provide safe interface for that.

**Describe the bug**
A clear and concise description of what the bug is.

the output of `INTERVAL XXX` is inconsistent

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

while we only have year or month, `it outputs IntervalYearMonth`
```bash
❯ select interval '1 year';
+------------------------------------------------+
| IntervalYearMonth("12")                        |
+------------------------------------------------+
| 1 years 0 mons 0 days 0 hours 0 mins 0.00 secs |
+------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set. Query took 0.001 seconds.
❯ select interval '1 year 1 month';
+------------------------------------------------+
| IntervalYearMonth("13")                        |
+------------------------------------------------+
| 1 years 1 mons 0 days 0 hours 0 mins 0.00 secs |
+------------------------------------------------+
```

while we have (year or month) and any other unit, it outputs `IntervalMonthDayNano`
```bash
+--------------------------------------------------------+
| IntervalMonthDayNano("950737950189618795196236955648") |
+--------------------------------------------------------+
| 0 years 12 mons 1 days 0 hours 0 mins 0.00 secs        |
+--------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set. Query took 0.001 seconds.
❯ select interval '1 year 1 second';
+--------------------------------------------------------+
| IntervalMonthDayNano("950737950171172051123527404032") |
+--------------------------------------------------------+
| 0 years 12 mons 0 days 0 hours 0 mins 1.00 secs        |
+--------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set. Query took 0.001 seconds.
```

Otherwise, it outputs `IntervalDaytime`
```bash
❯ select interval '1 second';
+------------------------------------------------+
| IntervalDayTime("1000")                        |
+------------------------------------------------+
| 0 years 0 mons 0 days 0 hours 0 mins 1.00 secs |
+------------------------------------------------+

+------------------------------------------------+
| IntervalDayTime("4294968296")                  |
+------------------------------------------------+
| 0 years 0 mons 1 days 0 hours 0 mins 1.00 secs |
+------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set. Query took 0.001 seconds.
```

**Expected behavior**
A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.

they should be consistent, as our current Timestamp is in nanosecond, i suggest using `IntervalMonthDayNano`. We could consider add functions to output specific data type(i.e. `to_interval_monthdaynano()`, `to_interval_daytime()`, `interval_yearmonth()` . But i think they might need different arithmetics

raw_text:
Binary expression canonical names are incorrect in some cases

**Describe the bug**
Consider the following two expressions, which are not the same:

```rust
let expr1 = expr1.and(expr2.or(expr3));
let expr2 = expr1.and(expr2).or(expr3);
```

They both produce the same string from `canonical_name`:

```sql
a < Int32(1) AND b < Int32(2) OR c < Int32(3)
```

This is not only confusing when reading plans but could also lead to optimization rules altering plans to have different semantics.

**To Reproduce**


**Expected behavior**
They should produce different results:

`expr1.and(expr2.or(expr3))` should produce:

```sql
a < Int32(1) AND (b < Int32(2) OR c < Int32(3))
```

`expr1.and(expr2).or(expr3)` should produce either of these:

```sql
a < Int32(1) AND b < Int32(2) OR c < Int32(3)
(a < Int32(1) AND b < Int32(2)) OR c < Int32(3)
```

There are two ways of resolving this:

- We could just wrap every binary expression in parentheses (easier to implement but makes expressions harder to read)
- We could make the logic precedence-aware so that parentheses are only inserted when needed (preferred)

**Additional context**

Upcast types during union schema creation.

**Describe the bug**
A clear and concise description of what the bug is.
When I run the query below on postgre
```sql
SELECT c1, c9 FROM aggregate_test_100 
UNION ALL 
SELECT c1, c3 FROM aggregate_test_100
```
where c9 has type `Bigint` and c3 has type `smallint`. It produces a valid result. However, when I run the above query on datafusion where c9 has type `Uint32` and c3 has type `Int8`.
It gives the error `ArrowError(CastError("Can't cast value 1491205016 to type Int8"))`.
The physical plan of the query above in DataFusion is as follows
```sql
"UnionExec",
"  ProjectionExec: expr=[c1@0 as c1, c3@1 as c3]",
"    CsvExec: files={1 group: [[Users/akurmustafa/projects/synnada/arrow-datafusion-tmp/testing/data/csv/aggregate_test_100.csv]]}, has_header=true, limit=None, projection=[c1, c3]",
"  ProjectionExec: expr=[c1@0 as c1, CAST(c9@1 AS Int8) as c3]",
"    CsvExec: files={1 group: [[Users/akurmustafa/projects/synnada/arrow-datafusion-tmp/testing/data/csv/aggregate_test_100.csv]]}, has_header=true, limit=None, projection=[c1, c9]",
```

Datafusion coerces the types `DataType::Uint32` and `DataType::Int8` to `DataType::Int8`. For instance we may choose to upcast types to `DataType::Int64` for this specific case.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
One can run query above

**Expected behavior**
A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.
I expect above query to work

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.

Improve performance if IN list function

*Note*: migrated from original JIRA: https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/ARROW-11182

The initial implementation of IN and NOT IN followed the "functional first, and then fast"

There are several potential performance improvements for the IN and NOT IN implementation in Data fusion such as optimizing for large lists (use a hash table rather than repeated comparisons) and short circuiting results. 

There are a bunch of good ideas in the comments on this PR: https://github.com/apache/arrow/pull/9038/files

WithBundle missing WorldQuery implementation

While fiddling with bundles, I wanted to do `Query<(My, Components), WithBundle<MyBundle>>`
but instead I'm met with this compilation error: 

```rust
error: the trait `WorldQuery` is not implemented for `bevy::prelude::WithBundle<CattleFarmBundle>` 
```

According to @TehPers, it might only need this

```rust
impl<T: Bundle> WorldQuery for WithBundle<T> {
    type Fetch = WithBundleFetch<T>;
    type State = WithBundleState<T>;
}
```

I was asked to create this issue, so here it is.

## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?
The most simple of systems require a lot of ugly boiler plate code such as:

```rust
#[derive(Query)]
pub struct PointMassQuery{
    position: &mut Position,
    momentum: &Momentum,
    mass: &Mass
```

Static type introspection

## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

It would be nice if I could get the names and types of fields in a struct, without creating an instance of that struct.

## What solution would you like?

Static methods on `Struct`, `Tuple`, etc. 

## What alternative(s) have you considered?

I could probably make my own macro to get just the info I need. It just feels like this is something that should be in a more general-purpose reflection crate.

## Additional context

My personal use case was an experimental entity-first ORM. I was hoping to use bevy_reflect to help generate migrations, but I needed this feature to make it work that way.

I already scrapped that whole idea in favor of a headless CMS, but I'm sure this would be useful for others.

Suggestion: Expose arg parsing programmatically / to libripgrep

In [rga](https://github.com/phiresky/ripgrep-all), I currently pass most arguments directly to ripgrep. But now I noticed I need to handle some of those flags myself, currently specifically --text, --binary, --null-data, --encoding, and their short versions to fix binary detection and [handle encodings](https://github.com/phiresky/ripgrep-all/issues/5).

In other words, a command given with `--pre` might also want to know about certain configuration options given to ripgrep itself.

If there was a way to access the clap App or even better the higher level configuration of ripgrep given a Vec<OsStr> of args, that would be great!

Currently, it looks like all of the arg parsing is in the ripgrep crate itself, which can't be loaded as a library, as far as I can tell.

Expose an API to determine whether a specific path is ignored

Hi all,
I have a use case where I want to determine whether a specific path is ignored, for example - I have a file watcher, and I want to determine whether or not to handle the incoming event with respect to the user's ignore configurations.
What are you guys recommending to do in my use case?

I started playing around with the `ignore` crate, and I think what I'm looking for is something along the lines of this function:
```rust
fn is_ignored(path: &Path) -> bool {
  let ig_root = IgnoreBuilder::new().build();
  let (ig, _err) = ig_root.add_parents(path);
  ig.matched(path, path.is_dir()).is_ignore()
}
```
I'm quite certain the code above is not 100% correct, so if you can provide some guidelines on how to implement it that'd be awsome.
I'll gladly open a PR with this API if you guys agree, and I'll be even happier if there is a way to handle my use case without changing any code :)

Kind regards and thanks in advance!

raw_text:
use `default_value_t` with `ArgEnum` without manually implementing `Display`

### Please complete the following tasks

- [X] I have searched the [discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Clap Version

master

### Describe your use case

deriving argenums with default values is currently a little clumsy, since you have to manually implement `Display`, and you need to manually ensure that the `Display` implementation is aligned with the derived `ArgEnum` implementation


for example

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Parser)]
pub struct List {

    #[clap(long, arg_enum, default_value_t]
    variant: Variant
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, ArgEnum)]
enum Variant {
    ObjectA,
    ObjectB
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Variant {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        let s = match self {
            Self::ObjectA => "object-a", // or is it "object_a"?
            Self::ObjectB => "object-b",
        };
        write!(f, "{}", s)
    }
}
```

what i'd *like* is to omit the manual `Display` implementation

### Describe the solution you'd like

`#[derive(ArgEnum)]` should generate a `Display` implementation which is consistent with the input values that it accepts

### Alternatives, if applicable

- `clap` provide a `Display` derive that is implemented in terms of `ArgEnum`
- Specialize `default_value_t` support for `ArgEnum`

### Additional Context

one possible edge case is that the derived `Display` implementation could conflict with another `Display` implementation (in which case `default_value_t` shouldn't be used anyway!)

therefore the generated `Display` implementation could have a flag to opt in or out (i would vote for making it opt out)

Some clap v3.x Subcommand derives cause clippy errors since Rust 1.69.0

### Please complete the following tasks

- [X] I have searched the [discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [X] I have searched the [open](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/issues) and [rejected](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AS-wont-fix+is%3Aclosed) issues

### Rust Version

rustc 1.69.0 (84c898d65 2023-04-16)

### Clap Version

clap 3.2.23, clap_derive 3.2.18

### Minimal reproducible code

```rust
#[derive(clap::Subcommand)]
enum Command {
    One,
}

fn main() {}
```


### Steps to reproduce the bug with the above code

Run clippy with defaults:

```sh
cargo clippy
```

### Actual Behaviour

This results in the following error in clippy.

```
error: this looks like you are trying to swap `__clap_subcommand` and `clap::Subcommand`
 --> src/main.rs:1:10
  |
1 | #[derive(clap::Subcommand)]
  |          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = note: or maybe you should use `std::mem::replace`?
  = help: for further information visit https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-clippy/master/index.html#almost_swapped
note: the lint level is defined here
 --> src/main.rs:1:10
  |
1 | #[derive(clap::Subcommand)]
  |          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  = note: `#[deny(clippy::almost_swapped)]` implied by `#[deny(clippy::correctness)]`
  = note: this error originates in the derive macro `clap::Subcommand` (in Nightly builds, run with -Z macro-backtrace for more info)

error: could not compile `clap-deny-correctness` due to previous error
```

### Expected Behaviour

The clippy error is problematic because the attribute that specifies `deny` is inside the macro itself. That means that as a user of Clap, I'm not able to override the deny.

Specifically this attribute:
```rust
#[deny(clippy::correctness)]
```

Which is present in 7 specific places in `clap_derive`.

### Additional Context

For Clap v4.x, these attributes were already removed in #4739.

Doing the same in the `v3-master` branch is probably sufficient

### Debug Output

_No response_

raw_text:
Combine long_flag and long_flag_aliases into one API?

Clap currently has https://docs.rs/clap/latest/clap/struct.Command.html#method.long_flag and https://docs.rs/clap/latest/clap/struct.Command.html#method.long_flag_aliases where `long_flag_aliases` does nothing without `long_flag` being specified. One could add a runtime warning/crash, but it's usually better to make bad states unrepresentable. ~~The proposed solution is to unify these APIs into a `long_flags` method.~~

Actually, the reason the "alias" method variants exist is to allow having hidden long flags that don't show up in help. I think the next best solution to use a builder pattern to only allow calling the alias variants after having specified the base long flag.

Infinitely recursing fish completion when 3 or more subcommand levels

### Please complete the following tasks

- [x] I have searched the [discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [x] I have searched the [open](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/issues) and [rejected](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AS-wont-fix+is%3Aclosed) issues

### Rust Version

rustc 1.86.0 (05f9846f8 2025-03-31)

### Clap Version

4.5.37

### Minimal reproducible code

```rust
use clap::{Args, CommandFactory, Parser, Subcommand};
use clap_complete::{generate, Shell};

#[derive(Parser)]
#[command(name = "clap_test", author, version, about)]
pub struct Cli {
    #[arg(long = "generate", hide = true, value_enum)]
    pub generator: Option<Shell>,

    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub command: Option<Commands>,
}

#[derive(Subcommand)]
pub enum Commands {
    First(FirstCommand),
}

#[derive(Args)]
pub struct FirstCommand {
    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub command: SecondCommand,
}

#[derive(Subcommand)]
pub enum SecondCommand {
    Second(SecondCommandArgs),
}

#[derive(Args)]
pub struct SecondCommandArgs {
    #[arg(long, short)]
    pub flag: bool,

    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub command: ThirdCommand,
}

#[derive(Subcommand)]
pub enum ThirdCommand {
    Third,
}

fn main() {
    let cli = Cli::parse();

    if let Some(generator) = cli.generator {
        let mut cmd = Cli::command();
        eprintln!("Generating completion file for {generator:?}...");
        let cmd = &mut cmd;
        generate(
            generator,
            cmd,
            cmd.get_name().to_string(),
            &mut std::io::stdout(),
        );
        return;
    }

    if let Some(Commands::First(first_command)) = cli.command {
        match first_command.command {
            SecondCommand::Second(second_command) => {
                match second_command.command {
                    ThirdCommand::Third {} => {
                        println!("Third command called");
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```


### Steps to reproduce the bug with the above code

```fish
# On the fish shell : 
# Build the CLI
cargo build
# Generate fish completions
cargo run -- --generate=fish > completions.fish
# Source fish completions
source completions.fish
# Trigger the completion on the third subcommand
./target/debug/clap_test first second third <TAB>
```

### Actual Behaviour

The fish shell display the following completion : 
```fish
❯ ./target/debug/clap_test first second third 
help  (Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s))  third
```

### Expected Behaviour

The fish shell **should** display the following completion : 
```fish
❯ ./target/debug/clap_test first second third 
Cargo.lock  Cargo.toml  completions.fish  src/  target/
```

### Additional Context

This same issue also occurs with arguments.

In this example there is a `flag` argument on the second command, the completion of the third command will display it as well : 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af71ddb2-e096-4c90-b0e0-b919bdbca933)

This issue is not present with the generated Bash completion.

Infinitely recursing fish completion when 3 or more subcommand levels

### Please complete the following tasks

- [x] I have searched the [discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [x] I have searched the [open](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/issues) and [rejected](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AS-wont-fix+is%3Aclosed) issues

### Rust Version

rustc 1.86.0 (05f9846f8 2025-03-31)

### Clap Version

4.5.37

### Minimal reproducible code

```rust
use clap::{Args, CommandFactory, Parser, Subcommand};
use clap_complete::{generate, Shell};

#[derive(Parser)]
#[command(name = "clap_test", author, version, about)]
pub struct Cli {
    #[arg(long = "generate", hide = true, value_enum)]
    pub generator: Option<Shell>,

    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub command: Option<Commands>,
}

#[derive(Subcommand)]
pub enum Commands {
    First(FirstCommand),
}

#[derive(Args)]
pub struct FirstCommand {
    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub command: SecondCommand,
}

#[derive(Subcommand)]
pub enum SecondCommand {
    Second(SecondCommandArgs),
}

#[derive(Args)]
pub struct SecondCommandArgs {
    #[arg(long, short)]
    pub flag: bool,

    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub command: ThirdCommand,
}

#[derive(Subcommand)]
pub enum ThirdCommand {
    Third,
}

fn main() {
    let cli = Cli::parse();

    if let Some(generator) = cli.generator {
        let mut cmd = Cli::command();
        eprintln!("Generating completion file for {generator:?}...");
        let cmd = &mut cmd;
        generate(
            generator,
            cmd,
            cmd.get_name().to_string(),
            &mut std::io::stdout(),
        );
        return;
    }

    if let Some(Commands::First(first_command)) = cli.command {
        match first_command.command {
            SecondCommand::Second(second_command) => {
                match second_command.command {
                    ThirdCommand::Third {} => {
                        println!("Third command called");
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Steps to reproduce the bug with the above code

```fish
# On the fish shell :
# Build the CLI
cargo build
# Generate fish completions
cargo run -- --generate=fish > completions.fish
# Source fish completions
source completions.fish
# Trigger the completion on the third subcommand
./target/debug/clap_test first second third <TAB>
```

### Actual Behaviour

The fish shell display the following completion :
```fish
❯ ./target/debug/clap_test first second third
help  (Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s))  third
```

### Expected Behaviour

The fish shell **should** display the following completion :
```fish
❯ ./target/debug/clap_test first second third
Cargo.lock  Cargo.toml  completions.fish  src/  target/
```

### Additional Context

This same issue also occurs with arguments.

In this example there is a `flag` argument on the second command, the completion of the third command will display it as well :

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af71ddb2-e096-4c90-b0e0-b919bdbca933)

This issue is not present with the generated Bash completion.

Infinitely recursing fish completion when 3 or more subcommand levels

### Please complete the following tasks

- [x] I have searched the [discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [x] I have searched the [open](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/issues) and [rejected](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AS-wont-fix+is%3Aclosed) issues

### Rust Version

rustc 1.86.0 (05f9846f8 2025-03-31)

### Clap Version

4.5.37

### Minimal reproducible code

```rust
use clap::{Args, CommandFactory, Parser, Subcommand};
use clap_complete::{generate, Shell};

#[derive(Parser)]
#[command(name = "clap_test", author, version, about)]
pub struct Cli {
    #[arg(long = "generate", hide = true, value_enum)]
    pub generator: Option<Shell>,

    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub command: Option<Commands>,
}

#[derive(Subcommand)]
pub enum Commands {
    First(FirstCommand),
}

#[derive(Args)]
pub struct FirstCommand {
    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub command: SecondCommand,
}

#[derive(Subcommand)]
pub enum SecondCommand {
    Second(SecondCommandArgs),
}

#[derive(Args)]
pub struct SecondCommandArgs {
    #[arg(long, short)]
    pub flag: bool,

    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub command: ThirdCommand,
}

#[derive(Subcommand)]
pub enum ThirdCommand {
    Third,
}

fn main() {
    let cli = Cli::parse();

    if let Some(generator) = cli.generator {
        let mut cmd = Cli::command();
        eprintln!("Generating completion file for {generator:?}...");
        let cmd = &mut cmd;
        generate(
            generator,
            cmd,
            cmd.get_name().to_string(),
            &mut std::io::stdout(),
        );
        return;
    }

    if let Some(Commands::First(first_command)) = cli.command {
        match first_command.command {
            SecondCommand::Second(second_command) => {
                match second_command.command {
                    ThirdCommand::Third {} => {
                        println!("Third command called");
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Steps to reproduce the bug with the above code

```fish
# On the fish shell :
# Build the CLI
cargo build
# Generate fish completions
cargo run -- --generate=fish > completions.fish
# Source fish completions
source completions.fish
# Trigger the completion on the third subcommand
./target/debug/clap_test first second third <TAB>
```

### Actual Behaviour

The fish shell display the following completion :
```fish
❯ ./target/debug/clap_test first second third
help  (Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s))  third
```

### Expected Behaviour

The fish shell **should** display the following completion :
```fish
❯ ./target/debug/clap_test first second third
Cargo.lock  Cargo.toml  completions.fish  src/  target/
```

### Additional Context

This same issue also occurs with arguments.

In this example there is a `flag` argument on the second command, the completion of the third command will display it as well :

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af71ddb2-e096-4c90-b0e0-b919bdbca933)

This issue is not present with the generated Bash completion.

Infinitely recursing fish completion when 3 or more subcommand levels

### Please complete the following tasks

- [x] I have searched the [discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [x] I have searched the [open](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/issues) and [rejected](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3AS-wont-fix+is%3Aclosed) issues

### Rust Version

rustc 1.86.0 (05f9846f8 2025-03-31)

### Clap Version

4.5.37

### Minimal reproducible code

```rust
use clap::{Args, CommandFactory, Parser, Subcommand};
use clap_complete::{generate, Shell};

#[derive(Parser)]
#[command(name = "clap_test", author, version, about)]
pub struct Cli {
    #[arg(long = "generate", hide = true, value_enum)]
    pub generator: Option<Shell>,

    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub command: Option<Commands>,
}

#[derive(Subcommand)]
pub enum Commands {
    First(FirstCommand),
}

#[derive(Args)]
pub struct FirstCommand {
    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub command: SecondCommand,
}

#[derive(Subcommand)]
pub enum SecondCommand {
    Second(SecondCommandArgs),
}

#[derive(Args)]
pub struct SecondCommandArgs {
    #[arg(long, short)]
    pub flag: bool,

    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub command: ThirdCommand,
}

#[derive(Subcommand)]
pub enum ThirdCommand {
    Third,
}

fn main() {
    let cli = Cli::parse();

    if let Some(generator) = cli.generator {
        let mut cmd = Cli::command();
        eprintln!("Generating completion file for {generator:?}...");
        let cmd = &mut cmd;
        generate(
            generator,
            cmd,
            cmd.get_name().to_string(),
            &mut std::io::stdout(),
        );
        return;
    }

    if let Some(Commands::First(first_command)) = cli.command {
        match first_command.command {
            SecondCommand::Second(second_command) => {
                match second_command.command {
                    ThirdCommand::Third {} => {
                        println!("Third command called");
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Steps to reproduce the bug with the above code

```fish
# On the fish shell :
# Build the CLI
cargo build
# Generate fish completions
cargo run -- --generate=fish > completions.fish
# Source fish completions
source completions.fish
# Trigger the completion on the third subcommand
./target/debug/clap_test first second third <TAB>
```

### Actual Behaviour

The fish shell display the following completion :
```fish
❯ ./target/debug/clap_test first second third
help  (Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s))  third
```

### Expected Behaviour

The fish shell **should** display the following completion :
```fish
❯ ./target/debug/clap_test first second third
Cargo.lock  Cargo.toml  completions.fish  src/  target/
```

### Additional Context

This same issue also occurs with arguments.

In this example there is a `flag` argument on the second command, the completion of the third command will display it as well :

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af71ddb2-e096-4c90-b0e0-b919bdbca933)

This issue is not present with the generated Bash completion.

Provide a `FromSql` impl for `*const str` and `*const [u8]`

There are various impls that compose on the `FromSql` impls for `String` and `Vec<u8>`, but do not need an owned string/vec. We cannot safely provide an impl for `&str`, or `&[u8]`. The only safe impl we could provide would be one where the return value lasts as long as the argument to `from_sql`. This would only  ever be useful for composed implementations, but providing that safe impl would require restructuring `FromSql` to have a lifetime attached, which I really don't want to do.

Though we can't represent the lifetime of this reference with the current structure of `FromSql`, we can absolutely provide an impl for raw pointers, documenting how long they last.

BoxableExpression for expressions including multiple tables?

I need to dynamically construct an expression which refers columns in different tables, specifically, to do something like
```sql
SELECT *
FROM table1
WHERE EXISTS(
  SELECT *
  FROM table2
  WHERE table2.field = table1.field AND whatever
)
```
This condition in the nested WHERE is supposed to be dynamic, depending on the user input. Unfortunately, `BoxableExpression` requires the implementing expression to be `SelectableExpression`, which effectively requires it to reference only a single table.

What is the suggested way to do this? Unfortunately, the queries in my case are rather complex, and I'd like not to fall back to `into_boxed()` on the queries level.

These compiler error messages are so hideous

### Versions
Diesel 1.4.5, features: sqlite
Rust 2018
Ubuntu 18.04

### Feature Flags
sqlite

## Problem Description
These compiler errors I see for diesel are some of the most confusing and difficult to solve.  Here is an example. 

> the trait bound `Sqlite: SupportsReturningClause` is not satisfied
> required because of the requirements on the impl of `QueryFragment<Sqlite>` for `diesel::query_builder::returning_clause::ReturningClause<(columns::id, columns::title, columns::published, columns::description, columns::name, columns::lbry_url)>`
> 1 redundant requirements hidden
> required because of the requirements on the impl of `QueryFragment<Sqlite>` for `InsertStatement<table, ValuesClause<(ColumnInsertValue<columns::title, diesel::expression::bound::Bound<diesel::sql_types::Text, &&str>>, ColumnInsertValue<columns::description, diesel::expression::bound::Bound<diesel::sql_types::Text, &&str>>, ColumnInsertValue<columns::name, diesel::expression::bound::Bound<diesel::sql_types::Nullable<diesel::sql_types::Text>, &&str>>), table>, diesel::query_builder::insert_statement::Insert, diesel::query_builder::returning_clause::ReturningClause<(columns::id, columns::title, columns::published, columns::description, columns::name, columns::lbry_url)>>`
> required because of the requirements on the impl of `LoadQuery<diesel::SqliteConnection, _>` for `InsertStatement<table, ValuesClause<(ColumnInsertValue<columns::title, diesel::expression::bound::Bound<diesel::sql_types::Text, &&str>>, ColumnInsertValue<columns::description, diesel::expression::bound::Bound<diesel::sql_types::Text, &&str>>, ColumnInsertValue<columns::name, diesel::expression::bound::Bound<diesel::sql_types::Nullable<diesel::sql_types::Text>, &&str>>), table>>

Errors like this pop up on the dsl function calls like load() and save_changes() and get_result().  This last one was on get_result, I fixed the issue with the other two.  

On the error on load() the issue had to do with my model having the wrong type, whereas on save_changes() the error was actually with my return type of my function.  The confusing thing is these messages all look the same and they all don't tell me the problem in a way I can understand.  Maybe this is something within your control to make better in future releases?

NOTE: I'm not asking to have this specific error solved, I'm just making a request / suggestion to somehow find a way to play nicer with the compiler and make the error messages make more sense.  Thanks for reading, carry on.

Using diesel CLI with `exclude_custom_type_definitions` has unexpected outcomes

## Setup

### Versions

- **Rust: 1.78**
- **Diesel: 2.2.0**
- **Database: Postgres**
- **Operating System: MacOS**

### Feature Flags

- **diesel:** `["postgres", "serde_json", "chrono", "uuid"]`

## Problem Description

### What are you trying to accomplish?

Generating a schema that uses the Geometry SQL types from postgis-diesel. Using the feature `exclude_custom_type_definitions` introduced with https://github.com/diesel-rs/diesel/pull/4002 and documented with https://diesel.rs/guides/configuring-diesel-cli.html#the-exclude_custom_type_definitions-field.

### What is the expected output?

No custom definition and an import of the postgis-diesel type(s).

### What is the actual output?

The custom definition is created and rather than saving output to `src/schema.rs` a new file is created with the name of the value of `exclude_custom_type_definitions`.

### Are you seeing any additional errors?

No additional errors. Patching the documentation or the CLI configuration to align would be great. Diesel CLI saving to a filename other than configured is also worthwhile fixing. 

### Steps to reproduce

Use a `diesel.toml` configured as below. Then run `diesel migration redo`.

```toml
[print_schema]
file = "src/schema.rs"
custom_type_derives = ["diesel::query_builder::QueryId"]
import_types = ["diesel::sql_types::*", "postgis_diesel::sql_types::*"]
exclude_custom_type_definitions = ["Geometry"]
```

To get the desired output `except_custom_type_definitions` has to be used rather than `exclude_custom_type_definitions`. This will properly save output to `src/schema.rs` and will use the postgis-diesel type.

Use a tuple with deserialize_as

Index is Being Copied to style.css when index_on_404 path is executed

**Problem**

<!-- A clear and concise description of what the bug is. -->

When I refresh a naively nested page that is not the index page on localhost while using `dx serve` the contents of style.css (my projects local stylesheet) are being overwritten by the contents of index.html.

One note is that this seems to only happen when naively nesting routes in the router. That is to say that it only happens when you hard code the nesting rather than using a #[nest] macro.

eg:
```rust
#[derive(Routable, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[rustfmt::skip]
pub enum Route {
    #[layout(NavBar)]
        #[route("/")]
        Home {},
        #[route("/about", About)]
        About {},
        #[route("/projects", Projects)]
        Projects{},
        #[route("/projects/alarm-clock")]
        AlarmClock {},
    #[end_layout]
    #[route("/:..route")]
    PageNotFound { route: Vec<String> },
}
```


**Steps To Reproduce**

Project Setup:
```toml
# Dioxus.toml
[application]

# App name
name = "baxterjo_webapp"

# The Dioxus platform to default to
default_platform = "web"

# `build` & `serve` output path
out_dir = "docs"

# The static resource path
asset_dir = "public"

[web.app]

# HTML title tag content
title = "Jordan Baxter"

[web.watcher]

# When watcher is triggered, regenerate the `index.html`
reload_html = true
index_on_404 = true

# Which files or dirs will be monitored
watch_path = ["src", "public", "public/css"]

# Include style or script assets
[web.resource]

# CSS style file
style = [
    "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.0.2/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css",
    "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@fortawesome/fontawesome-free@6.4.2/css/fontawesome.min.css",
    "https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Montserrat:300,400,500,700",
    "css/style.css",
]

# Javascript code file
script = [
    "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.0.2/dist/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js",
]

[web.resource.dev]

# Same as [web.resource], but for development servers

# CSS style file
style = []

# JavaScript files
script = []

[[web.proxy]]
backend = "http://localhost:8000/api/"
```

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
- Setup a web project that has a `style.css` in the public directory. Mine is under `public/css/style.css`
- Make the include of that stylesheet the last in your list of stylesheets in `Dioxus.toml` (I'm not sure if this has an effect, but it is how mine is setup.)
- Setup a router like above
- Run `dx serve` with or without the `--hot-reload` option
- Navigate to "/projects/alarm-clock" or similar nested route
- Hit refresh
- If your style.css file has any selectors that apply to this page you should see a change
- Open page inspector and navigate to the style editor
- Scroll down to style.css, file should have the contents of index.html in it

**Expected behavior**

If using the nest macro is required for nested paths, compilation should fail on the router with a message that tells the user to use the `#[nest]` macro.

If using the nest macro is not required, then the router should route the user to the correct page with no issues.

**Screenshots**

**Problem**

When I refresh a naively nested page that is not the index page on localhost while using `dx serve` the contents of style.css (my projects local stylesheet) are being overwritten by the contents of index.html.

One note is that this seems to only happen when naively nesting routes in the router. That is to say that it only happens when you hard code the nesting rather than using a #[nest] macro.

eg:
```rust
#[derive(Routable, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[rustfmt::skip]
pub enum Route {
    #[layout(NavBar)]
        #[route("/")]
        Home {},
        #[route("/about", About)]
        About {},
        #[route("/projects", Projects)]
        Projects{},
        #[route("/projects/alarm-clock")]
        AlarmClock {},
    #[end_layout]
    #[route("/:..route")]
    PageNotFound { route: Vec<String> },
}
```

**Steps To Reproduce**

Project Setup:
```toml
# Dioxus.toml
[application]

# App name
name = "baxterjo_webapp"

# The Dioxus platform to default to
default_platform = "web"

# `build` & `serve` output path
out_dir = "docs"

# The static resource path
asset_dir = "public"

[web.app]

# HTML title tag content
title = "Jordan Baxter"

[web.watcher]

# When watcher is triggered, regenerate the `index.html`
reload_html = true
index_on_404 = true

# Which files or dirs will be monitored
watch_path = ["src", "public", "public/css"]

# Include style or script assets
[web.resource]

# CSS style file
style = [
    "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.0.2/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css",

    "https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Montserrat:300,400,500,700",
    "css/style.css",
]

# Javascript code file
script = [
    "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.0.2/dist/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js",
]

[web.resource.dev]

# Same as [web.resource], but for development servers

# CSS style file
style = []

# JavaScript files
script = []

[[web.proxy]]
backend = "http://localhost:8000/api/"
```

Stack overflow/segfault when calling `peak` on `Loader` (web/desktop)

**Problem**

Calling `peak` on `Loader` causes segfault/stack overflow
According to GDB stack trace, these functions are called in a loop:
```
dioxus_fullstack_core::loader::{impl#2}::try_peek_unchecked<alloc::string::String> (self=0x5555575cb420)
dioxus_signals::read::ReadableExt::peek_unchecked<dioxus_fullstack_core::loader::Loader<alloc::string::String>> (self=0x5555575cb420)
```
On desktop, this results in a segmentation fault; on the web, it causes a stack overflow.

**Steps To Reproduce**

```rust
use dioxus::prelude::*;

fn main() {
    dioxus::launch(App);
}

#[component]
fn App() -> Element {
    let data = use_loader(data)?;

    use_effect(move || { data.peek(); });

    rsx! {
        "{data:?}"
    }
}

#[get("/api/data")]
async fn data() -> Result<String, ServerFnError> {
    Ok("data".to_string())
}
```

**Expected behavior**

Should not cause stack overflow.

**Environment:**

- Dioxus version:  `v0.7.1` / `main (2a515a3)`
- Rust version:    `1.92.0-nightly`
- App platform:    `desktop`/`web`

It appears to be a minor bug in the try_peek_unchecked implementation for Loader.
I managed to get it working correctly with this change:

```diff
diff --git a/packages/fullstack-core/src/loader.rs b/packages/fullstack-core/src/loader.rs
index 8a4a6b23a..f5aa61f6e 100644
--- a/packages/fullstack-core/src/loader.rs
+++ b/packages/fullstack-core/src/loader.rs
@@ -238,7 +238,7 @@ impl<T> Readable for Loader<T> {
     where
         T: 'static,
     {
-        Ok(self.peek_unchecked())
+        Ok(self.read_value.peek_unchecked())
     }

     fn subscribers(&self) -> Subscribers
```

Thank you

Link error with embassy-time `std` after ETQU 0.3.1 update

In my app using tokio as executor on a windows host I observe following problem:

Cargo.toml
``` toml
[dependencies]
# ...
embassy-time = { version = "0.5.1", features = ["std", "generic-queue-64"] }
# ...
```

```
error: linking with `link.exe` failed: exit code: 1120
...
  = note: libembassy_executor_timer_queue-bf561fbb86a3a64d.rlib(embassy_executor_timer_queue-bf561fbb86a3a64d.embassy_executor_timer_queue.1e351648231269a7-cgu.0.rcgu.o) : error LNK2019: unresolved external symbol __embassy_time_queue_item_from_waker referenced in function _ZN28embassy_executor_timer_queue14TimerQueueItem18from_embassy_waker17hf61ae3dbb1e813d9E
          C:\myapp.exe : fatal error LNK1120: 1 unresolved externals
```

When I pin ETQU with `cargo update -p embassy-time-queue-utils --precise 0.3.0` everything builds fine again.

To me this looks like for whatever reason the new ETQU tries to use the integrated timer queue instead of a generic one as selected by the `embassy-time` feature.

When changing the text selection inside a TextEdit by dragging the mouse, the TextSelectionChanged event is never emitted.

The event is emitted.

**Additional context**

This is because state.cursor.char_range() must be saved before running the state.cursor.pointer_interaction.

Touch position mismatch in split screen (Android)

**Describe the bug**
I'm using egui (0.32) + egui_winit + egui_wgpu.
On Android, when using split-screen feature in an egui app, the visible content doesn't match the touch position. This happens because the app is running fullscreen, but in split-screen mode the android top bar is always visible, offsetting the visible ui content, but touch events still occur as if the app was running in fullscreen mode.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Expand your android egui app to fullscreen (hide the system topbar)
2. Test the app, the buttons should click where you place your finger
3. Switch to split screen mode. The app is now displayed at half size, the top bar is visible
4. The ui is now shifted down by the size of the top bar. Taps cause misses

**Expected behavior**
Touch events are accurate regardless of the visibility of the android top bar

**Smartphone (please complete the following information):**
 - Device: Samsung Galaxy A52 5G
 - OS: Android 14

raw_text:
WGPU buffers not deallocated when minimised

**Describe the bug**
WGPU buffer garbage collection is dependent on `wgpu::Queue::submit()`. When minimised this is not called because `egui_wgpu::winit::Painter::paint_and_update_textures()` returns early due to `SurfaceErrorAction::SkipFrame`. Any allocated wgpu buffers aren't destroyed, and any allocations build up indefinitely until out of GPU memory.
Most egui applications don't allocate much per frame and don't perform receive events/redraw while minimised, so this isn't usually noticeable.
The memory usage can be observed with `<eframe::CreationContext>.wgpu_render_state.device.get_internal_counters().hal.buffer_memory.read();`.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Checkout https://github.com/nickd-airo/egui_mwe.
   - Egui window which only draws a label
   - Renders continuously using request_repaint()
   - It uses wgpu backend, and the wgpu counters feature to track buffer memory
   - It prints the buffer memory counter on every frame.
3. Run the app.
4. Observe the idle memory.
5. Minimise the app.
6. Observe the memory usage growing.
7. Unminimise the app.
8. Observe the memory usage return to normal.

**Desktop**
 - OS: Windows

**Additional context**
For a [minimal example](https://github.com/nickd-airo/egui_mwe), when window is not minimised, usage is 581728 bytes and does not change.
After minimising, usage grows linearly, and after ~30s, memory usage is 6221920 bytes. (188 kB/sec).
When unminimised, the memory usage returns to 581728 immediately.

I'm working on an app with a 3D scene inside egui, and it crashes ~20m after being minimised with 20GB of GPU memory (Normal usage is <3GB), and after even 1m of being minimised, has a significant delay from freeing memory.

It seems like `wgpu::Device::poll()` can also perform the required cleanup.

raw_text:
Bitflags in API traces are hard to write and read

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When writing a playtest or reading an API trace, it's difficult to reason about bitflag values. See https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/pull/1191/files#diff-78d438d1c2e726454851597e74ab167a9579d6cd83d7f712fcea59173cc2b274R27 for example.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Something like https://github.com/kvark/bitflags-serial, where the flags are serialized as `VALUE | ANOTHER_VALUE`
Another alternative is to turn them into structures like `Foo { bit_some: bool, bit_other: bool, ...}`, but that's more complicated.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Keep them integers but comment on each use...

**Additional context**
See upstream in https://github.com/bitflags/bitflags/issues/147
Is also a problem for gfx-rs Warden testing infra.

Validation error with atomic arrays on metal

**Description**
When running the `hello-compute` example with an atomic array (`array<atomic<u32>>`) I get a validation error. I'm not sure if this is how you're supposed to make an atomic array but the error didn't look right, so I tried it on windows with Vulkan. On windows, the atomics worked perfectly so I figured I should post a bug report. I can run some tests if you don't have access to a mac.

**Repro steps**
On macOS, m1 chip, metal backend

In shader.wgsl change
```rust
struct PrimeIndices {
    data: [[stride(4)]] array<u32>;
};
```
to
```rust
struct PrimeIndices {
    data: [[stride(4)]] array<atomic<u32>>;
};
```
and add `atomicAdd(&v_indices.data[global_id.x], 1u);` to the main function.

**Expected vs observed behaviour**
```
thread 'main' panicked at 'wgpu error: Validation Error

Caused by:
    In Device::create_compute_pipeline
    Internal error: Metal: program_source:58:49: error: cannot take the address of an rvalue of type 'metal::uint' (aka 'unsigned int')
    uint _e6 = metal::atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&metal::uint(_e3) < 1 + (_buffer_sizes.size0 - 0 - 4) / 4 ? v_indices.data[_e3] : DefaultConstructible(), 1u, metal::memory_order_relaxed);
```

**Platform**
wgpu version 0.12

**Description**
When using `copy_texture_to_texture` with the webGL2 backend and array textures I get invalid data displayed. It's hard to tell exactly what is going wrong since I can't really debug the code. I tried SpectorJS but it does not show individual textures.

**Repro steps**
Clone:
https://github.com/StarArawn/bevy_ecs_tilemap

Run(wasm/webGL2/array texture):
```
cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --example iso_diamond --release
wasm-server-runner .\target\wasm32-unknown-unknown\release\examples\iso_diamond.wasm
```

Run(wasm/webGL2/atlas):
```
cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --example iso_diamond --release --features atlas
wasm-server-runner .\target\wasm32-unknown-unknown\release\examples\iso_diamond.wasm
```

Run(desktop)
```
cargo run --example iso_diamond
```

**Expected vs observed behavior**
Compare with the desktop or atlas versions and you can see the issue.

**Extra materials**
None

**Platform**
Chrome/WebGL2

Vulkan validation errors

<!-- Thank you for filing this! Please read the [debugging tips](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/wiki/Debugging-wgpu-Applications).
That may let you investigate on your own, or provide additional information that helps us to assist.-->

**Description**
Vulkan validation errors every frame.

**Repro steps**
Any wgpu examples that render something (water or cube for example)

**Expected vs observed behavior**
I would expect no validation errors.\
The rendering is still perfectly fine.

**Extra materials**

Message that are spammed every frame (examples that render only one frame (hello-triangle) only log this once):
```
[2023-08-11T12:32:44Z ERROR wgpu_hal::vulkan::instance] VALIDATION [VUID-VkRenderPassBeginInfo-framebuffer-04627 (0x45125641)]
        Validation Error: [ VUID-VkRenderPassBeginInfo-framebuffer-04627 ] Object 0: handle = 0x3a6cbb0000000025, type = VK_OBJECT_TYPE_RENDER_PASS; | MessageID = 0x45125641 | vkCmdBeginRenderPass: Image view #0 created from an image with usage set as (VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT|VK_IMAGE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT) but using VkImageViewUsageCreateInfo the inherited usage is the subset (VK_IMAGE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT) and the image info #0 used to create the framebuffer had usage set as (VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT|VK_IMAGE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT). The Vulkan spec states: If framebuffer was created with a VkFramebufferCreateInfo::flags value that included VK_FRAMEBUFFER_CREATE_IMAGELESS_BIT, each element of the pAttachments member of a VkRenderPassAttachmentBeginInfo structure included in the pNext chain must be a VkImageView with an inherited usage equal to the usage member of the corresponding element of VkFramebufferAttachmentsCreateInfo::pAttachmentImageInfos used to create framebuffer (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/1.3.239.0/windows/1.3-extensions/vkspec.html#VUID-VkRenderPassBeginInfo-framebuffer-04627)
[2023-08-11T12:32:44Z ERROR wgpu_hal::vulkan::instance]                                                    objects: (type: RENDER_PASS, hndl: 0x3a6cbb0000000025, name: ?)
```

**Platform**
Windows 10\
Wgpu 0.16.3

raw_text:
`GlobalVariable` does not provide a way to determine if it is a builtin or not

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
My [rust backend](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/pull/5175) needs to translate global variables like `gl_FragCoord` to different names and attributes. The entrypoint attributes work fine, as I can go from `EntryPoint` to `FunctionArgument`s which have a `Binding` that is set to `Binding::BuiltIn(b: BuiltIn)` if the argument is a builtin.

When code is _using_ or referring to a built-in, it appears in the IR as a `GlobalVariable`. Unfortunately, there is no way to go from `GlobalVariable` to `Binding::BuiltIn`. `GlobalVariable` has a binding, but it is a `ResourceBinding` which only has an index and a group.

The problem arises because at _definition time_ the backend gets a `BuiltIn` for the `EntryPoint` `FunctionArg` but there is no name, and at _usage time_ the backend only has the name with no builtin info. It cannot make the two match without   passing around the input format to infer the global name to use as the `EntryPoint` argument name.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
1. Have `Binding` on `GlobalVariable`. I do not know enough about shaders / naga to determine if `Binding` gives all information needed and can replace `ResourceBinding`. 
2. Have the entrypoint argument name not be empty. It should be set to the correct name for the `BuiltIn` in the input format. Then the `Namer` can handle everything.

I _think_ I prefer the second option, but I don't know which is more appropriate. I think just doing the second option means I can have rename rules that rename based on the closed set of GLSL global strings (for example, chop off "gl_"), but I can't generate entirely new names based on the builtin type / have the generated name be frontend-agnostic (again, the calling location only has the name not the builtin's type). Doing both 1 and 2 would provide maximum flexibility and information to the backends.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
* I think globals will never have a `ResourceBinding` so I can indirectly key off that to determine if it is a builtin? Sadly, I'd have to store a brittle mapping of the string name to the `Builtin` as there would be no way to get the _specific_ builtin.

**Additional context**
Happy to put up a PR if someone points me in the right direction.

[naga-cli] Use of `--stdin-file-path` prevents writing output files

<!-- Thank you for filing this! Please read the [debugging tips](https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/wiki/Debugging-wgpu-Applications).
That may let you investigate on your own, or provide additional information that helps us to assist.-->

**Description**
It's impossible to translate stdin files with naga-cli and specify the output file. It looks like the switch for parsing the ``--stdin-file-path`` argument is only invoked if the first file argument is Some: ``args.files.first()``.  However, this means that it's actually impossible to have naga translate a file from stdin.

**Repro steps**
```
$cat file.wgsl | naga --input-kind wgsl --stdin-file-path file.wgsl file.spv
```

**Expected vs observed behavior**
Using ``stdin-file-path`` should not cause naga to treat the first file name in the argument list as an input file.

raw_text:
Simpler way to transform response body, `response.deconstruct()`

If you want to transform a response's body, there doesn't seem to be a nice way to consume the old response into a new response but with a different body. For example, this isn't so great:

```rust
let response2 = Response::new()
    .with_status(response.status().clone())
    .with_headers(response.headers().clone())
    .with_body(transform(response.body()))
```

Looking around hyper's code, it looks like `hyper::proto::response::{from_wire, split}` are ideal, but they are private functions. But this is exactly what I want to do in middleware:

```rust
use hyper::proto::response::{from_wire, split};

let (head, body) = split(response);
let response2 = from_wire(head, transform(body))
```

I'm not super experienced, so I might be missing something that suits my fancy. But so far `response.body()` has been a nuisance because it consumes the response but only moves out the body.

Moving the status, headers, and body out of the response in one go, like `Request#deconstruct()`, and a way to construct them back into a response would be much more helpful in middleware.

raw_text: Bad tail latency: always-ready connection can starve others We compare a [hyper hello-world server](https://github.com/denoland/deno/blob/3dff147d0ca1a2cd8d264d20a178d71cb38b1c4e/tools/hyper_hello.rs)'s performance against our own (dynamic language) web server. We've noticed that hyper has very bad tail latency - sometimes as much as 2 seconds. You can see it here https://deno.land/benchmarks.html#max-latency We debugged this a bit, thinking at first it was our setup. But concluded that it was indeed a bug in hyper after making these changes: https://github.com/denoland/deno_third_party/compare/1902aba524c96f56c1dd654f04660a1fc3ebf80d...d8fb68ccfb72ad6a8b306dfcc3573efafa3c340f cc @piscisaureus @carllerche

raw_text:
OpenGL backend does not work on old OpenGL hardware (e.g. OpenGL ES 2)

The current OpenGL (glow) backend does not work on OpenGL ES 2 hardware (such as the PinePhone [Mali 400 GPU] in my case, with the latest GLSL version supported being 1.20).

However, it's not too far from being able to run there. By removing the use of instanced rendering and switching to older GLSL syntax, I managed to get it running on my PinePhone.

I have a fork at https://bics.ga/reivilibre/iced-mobile/src/commit/2dc42b4a22ffc31a83297bfed7641e3737a0a940 which I am using .

I'm not sure if I can contribute any changes back immediately (since there may be a performance cost for hardware which does support instanced rendering etc, but I felt compelled to leave a note here in case anyone may find it useful.

(as an aside: I have left a comment about my experience with Iced on the PinePhone on the mobile issue here: https://github.com/hecrj/iced/issues/302#issuecomment-869061787)

I wonder what the best approach might be here; would we prefer to have both a modern implementation and an old one and use the modern one if we can?

However, it's not too far from being able to run there. By removing the use of instanced rendering and switching to older GLSL syntax, I managed to get it running on my PinePhone.

I have a fork at https://bics.ga/reivilibre/iced-mobile/src/commit/2dc42b4a22ffc31a83297bfed7641e3737a0a940 which I am using .

I'm not sure if I can contribute any changes back immediately (since there may be a performance cost for hardware which does support instanced rendering etc, but I felt compelled to leave a note here in case anyone may find it useful.

(as an aside: I have left a comment about my experience with Iced on the PinePhone on the mobile issue here: https://github.com/hecrj/iced/issues/302#issuecomment-869061787)

I wonder what the best approach might be here; would we prefer to have both a modern implementation and an old one and use the modern one if we can?

WASM: text inside row![] inside button() clips to single character

## Description

When targeting `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, placing a `row![]` with multiple `text()` widgets inside a `button()` causes the text content to be clipped to a single character. This does not occur on native (Linux/Vulkan).

## Reproduction

```rust
// BROKEN on WASM — shows "I" instead of "Import"
button(
    row![
        text(icon_char).font(icon_font).size(16),
        text("Import").size(13),
    ]
    .spacing(6)
    .align_y(Alignment::Center)
)
.padding([6, 12])
.width(Length::Fill)
.style(primary_button_style)

// WORKS on WASM — shows full "Import"
button(
    text("Import").size(13).center()
)
.padding([6, 12])
.width(Length::Fill)
.style(primary_button_style)
```

## Observations

- Single `text()` inside `button()` renders correctly on WASM
- `row![]` inside `button()` causes text to clip to 1 character on WASM
- Same code renders correctly on native (Linux, Vulkan backend)
- `.width(Length::Fill)` on the button may be a contributing factor, but removing it still shows the clipping when `row![]` is present
- `text()` with explicit `.font()` is not the cause — tested with default font and explicit font, both clip inside `row![]`
- `row![]` outside of `button()` (e.g., in a `container`) renders text correctly

## Environment

- iced 0.14
- Target: `wasm32-unknown-unknown`
- Built with trunk 0.21.14
- Browser: Chrome (WebGPU enabled)
- Works correctly on: Linux native (Vulkan)

## Workaround

Use a single `text()` widget inside `button()` instead of `row![]`. For buttons that need an icon + label, either concatenate them in one string or place them outside the button.

Long Compile Times: Dynamic Linking?

I've used the Bevy game engine and I cannot live without the super fast (sometimes <1 second!) dynamic linking support. Is this possible to do with Iced? Being a UI library, Iced applications need lots of design iteration for styling & layout. However, iteration is made tedious with long compile times. Is it possible to implement a feature similar to Bevy's `--features bevy/dynamic`?

PR for this Issue: #867

Type safe search params in router

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
It is often recommended to use search params as state, however it is often difficult to pull off in big systems because the link tag don't know what search params the route expects. I ran across [tanstack router](https://tanstack.com/router/v1/docs/guide/search-params) which, among other great ideas, has type safe search params. So I was wondering if leptos could add support for something similar.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Looking at it, the tanstack router is quite a lot different from the leptos router, so I can't see immediately how the a-tag would know what search params the route would expect. But ideally the route would describe the expected type, perhaps just a struct that impl Deserialize, and then the a-tag would know the expected type.

Something like
```rust
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct UsersSearchParams {
  tab: Tab
}
// route
<Route path="/users" view=Users search=UsersSearchParams/>

// later when linking to the page
<A href="/users" search=UsersSearchParams {tab: Tab::Settings} />
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
The current solution is okay, as that is what the vast majority of routers out there use, but it would be cool to get type safe routes like this

Rewrite the protocol.rs file in Kademlia to be more straight-forward

The current `protocol.rs` is quite complex because of backwards-compatibility reasons from a time where we implemented the Kademlia is a way that's incompatible with go-libp2p and js-libp2p.

This was a very long time ago, and it should now be possible to remove this backwards compatibility code and replace it with more straight-forward code.
Inspiration can be taken from the `protocol.rs` file in `Floodsub`.

The current `protocol.rs` is quite complex because of backwards-compatibility reasons from a time where we implemented the Kademlia is a way that's incompatible with go-libp2p and js-libp2p.

This was a very long time ago, and it should now be possible to remove this backwards compatibility code and replace it with more straight-forward code.
Inspiration can be taken from the `protocol.rs` file in `Floodsub`.

Update the minimum version of `either` dependency from 1.5 to 1.8 in libp2p-core

## Summary

Seen in [this StackOverflow post](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76220673), the user updated libp2p from v0.46 to v0.53.1 which updated libp2p-core to v0.39.2 and experienced a compilation error within the library:

```
error[E0599]: no method named `as_pin_mut` found for struct `Pin<&mut either::Either<A, B>>` in the current scope
   --> <project>/vendor/crates/libp2p-core-0.39.2/src/either.rs:147:20
    |
147 |         match self.as_pin_mut() {
    |                    ^^^^^^^^^^ help: there is a method with a similar name: `as_mut`

For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0599`
```

The user reports the version of either was v1.6.1.

## Possible Solution

It seems [a recent change introduced calling `.as_pin_mut()` on a `either::Either`](https://github.com/libp2p/rust-libp2p/blob/3fde13220b29f0878d6f98a3fe50bc9b008baf8a/core/src/either.rs#L132), but this method only exists as of v1.8 which is higher than the required version of `"1.5"` [in the Cargo.toml](https://github.com/libp2p/rust-libp2p/blob/3fde13220b29f0878d6f98a3fe50bc9b008baf8a/core/Cargo.toml#L14).

So the fix would be to either revert that part of the change or update the minimum version of either to v1.8.

raw_text:
request-response: Document request/response max sizes

### Description

`cbor` and `json` codecs have [hard-coded req-resp max size](https://github.com/libp2p/rust-libp2p/blob/master/protocols/request-response/src/cbor.rs#L54-L57) that are not documentated.
I propose to document them at the [`Behaviour` section](https://docs.rs/libp2p/latest/libp2p/request_response/cbor/type.Behaviour.html)

### Motivation

Trying to send a too-big request [throw I/O errors](https://github.com/libp2p/rust-libp2p/blob/master/protocols/request-response/src/cbor.rs#L93) (like [`WriteZero`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/io/enum.ErrorKind.html#variant.WriteZero)) which is not always easy to understand (for beginner like me at least).
Having a documentation might help to understand the source of the issue when facing such errors.

### Current Implementation

No documentation

### Are you planning to do it yourself in a pull request ?

Yes

Make `trim` trim all columns and rows

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Right now the `trim` command expects to get a stream of strings to trim.  Often, though, when you really want to `trim` is when you have a table and the data has spaces around it.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
`trim` should be extended to work on rows as well as strings. For rows, it will go one-deep and trim the contents of each column, outputting the newly-trimmed rows.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could make a new command to do this, but I think extending `trim` is the most natural.

**Additional context**
You can find the current `trim` command in https://github.com/nushell/nushell/blob/master/crates/nu-cli/src/commands/trim.rs

Tests in: https://github.com/nushell/nushell/tree/master/crates/nu-cli/tests/commands (though it looks like `trim` doesn't have tests, yet, and we should add them)

No way of inclusive..exclusive ranges

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Current ranges, like `1..3` are inclusive on both ends, so what you get out would be 1, 2, 3.

It'd be nice to have a way of saying the right hand side was exclusive.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We can start out with an addition to the current syntax. Here's the first one that came to mind:

* `1..3` - 1, 2, 3
* `1..<3` - 1, 2

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
We could make exclusive right hand side the default and use `1..=3` like Rust
