raw_text:
Overhaul of Scope

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
This is a list of steps that work together to improve Scope, fix long-standing issues with scope leak, improve overall performance, and (hopefully) improve maintainability.

Currently, when a variable is accessed, we have to take a global lock to read or write its value. Likewise, when working with blocks, under certain circumstances we can see variables that should not be visible from the current scope.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

This solution works with a few different moving parts. I'll describe them in each section, though sections may refer forward and backward as different parts work together.

## Definitions

* Block - A block of code, which is output by the parser
* CapturedBlock - A Block that has a record that includes the values of the [captured variables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closure_(computer_programming)) of the block
* Scope - A lookup for finding definitions that can be seen inside the current block
* Stack frame - a frame of the stack representing the definitions/variables defined at this level of scope
* Block-Owned Stack Frame - A stack frame specific to the given block

## More use of interning

One current shortcoming is that we don't have an easy way to bind definitions to simple identifiers that we can later use when referencing these definitions. This means that for definitions, we end up copying around Block (or Arc<Block>) and for variables we end up always doing a Scope lookup (which today also incurs a lock).

What we should instead do is apply a good dose of interning logic.

### Block interning

Definitions can be interned into the global context because after parse time, we no longer edit the list of definitions. With this being the case, it should be able to safely live in an Arc and not need any locking.

By moving Blocks to be handled instead as BlockIds, we can more easily bind CallInfo to what is called rather than looking up the definition rather than needing to look up the current scope.

### Variable "interning"

While not exactly interning, what we can do with variables is to also convert them to a VarId. This removes the need, during eval, of having to look up the variable in the current scope.

Blocks either capture a variable or define a set of local variables. Captured variables would be slots in the current Block-Owned Scope Frame (See below). Local variables likewise would also have their own slots in the Block-Owned Scope Frame. This allows us to prepare a Block for evaluation by first copying in the values of the bound captures (which should themselves be available in the parent scope) into the slots provided for captures, and the local variable slots would be primed with an empty slot.

At this point, evaluation of the CapturedBlock no longer needs any access to scopes at all. Instead, blocks only need the EvaluationContext to perform the work.

**Note:** when handling captured values, we do still need to deep-copy the value of the variable at the time of capture, as the slot where the value comes from may have been filled with a new value by the time the CapturedBlock is later evaluated.

## Block-Owned Scope Frame

The Block, when parsed, will have knowledge of what variables it defines and which it captures. The combination allows us to create slots in a scope frame that will handle the captured variables and the local variables. These slots allow us to create local VarIds that are valid inside of the Block. These ids prevent having to lookup variable names in a scope. Instead, we would need only to use the VarId as an index into the vec held by the scope frame.

Parameters to blocks likewise will be given slots and held in the Block-Owned Scope Frame. To the Block, these parameters are just another variable during evaluation time. They just happen to be setup by the caller before the CapturedBlock gets evaluated.

Looking at an example:

```
let x = 3;
let foo = {|y|
  let z = 10
  $x + $y + $z
}
do $foo 7
```

Once parsed, we have this pseudo-code:
```
<set $x slot to 3>
```

The `foo` definition has a Block. This Block is turned into a BlockId during block interning (see above). When the `let foo = ...` line is run, we evaluate the Block expression, which gives us back a CapturedBlock value. This CapturedBlock contains the captured part of the frame we'll later use, along with the BlockId of the block to run. 

```
CapturedBlock {
  captures: [Value::int(3)]
  block_id: 1,
}
```

Next, when we run the block during `do $foo 7` we first setup the rest of the Block-Owned Scope Frame:

```
ScopeFrame {
  block: Box<CapturedBlock>
  vars: vec![],
}
```
The parameters are then pushed onto the vars, and we make space for the future vars:
```
ScopeFrame {
  block: Box<CapturedBlock>
  vars: vec![Value::int(7), Var::empty],
}
```
(we may want to improve this further in the future, so we don't spend time on pushing the unused empty)

Finally, once we're running the block, as the `let z = 10` is finally run, we get our final:

```
  vars: vec![Value::int(7), Var::int(10)],
```

You'll notice that the captured variables are split from the local variables. This is to prevent having to do extra copying when a block is invoked. Instead, we check the VarId, and if it is larger than the number of captures, we look for the variable as a local.

**Note:** At this point, we should already know the DefIds for all CallInfo sites. We don't need to manage them in the Scope during evaluation. Instead, this should all be resolved during parse time, using the parse-time scope.

## Mutability

Block-Owned Stack Frames must be mutable by `run_block`. Without this, there's no way to set variables with their values. To allow for this, we need to ensure that variable declaration **are the only thing in the pipeline** so that we can detect it and properly convert the Arc to a mutable reference for updates. We can relax this restriction after some experience with it, but the initial restriction is what allows us to be safe to mutate during runtime.

## Global parts of scope

There are a few parts of global scope that we currently mutate, including state specific to directory-specific environments. We can leave this as part of scope or move it into a protected place inside of EvaluationContext. If these need to be mutable, they'll need to remain protected by locks. If these can be set during parse time and then are later read-only, we should be able to use an Arc instead.

## Aliases

The logic for Aliases can follow similarly to Definitions. During parse time, we should know in advance that a call site will bind to an alias. Even more, we can fully expand this alias during parse time so that we do not need to handle aliases during evaluation time.

Some care needs to be taken to ensure we can give proper error spans if an expanded alias later fails to evaluate.

## Entering and exiting scopes

Under the current system, we manually enter and exit scopes. This allows us more fine-grained control of when we want to use the current scope or to start with a fresh scope frame (and fall back to parents when doing lookup).

With the above changes, all of this logic changes. Calls always go through the Block-Owned Scope Frame logic detailed above. There is no longer a notion of entering and exiting scopes. This has one exception, the use of imports like `source`, which is detailed below.

## Handling `source`

The `source` command has multiple duties in the current system. During parse time, the `source` command will load in the definitions available in the `source`-d file and put them into scope. During evaluation time, `source` will run the block given at the top-level of the `source`-d file. Let us explore each of these:

### `source` at parse time

Under this refactor, the parser will parse the `source`-d file, interning definitions it finds and granting new DefIds to their uses. It will track which of these DefIds are available in the current scope, so if, for example the user does:

```
source foo.nu
foo 3    # assuming `foo` is defined in foo.nu
```

Then the definition for `foo` provided by the "foo.nu" file will have a DefId visible to anyone who wants to bind to it at the current scope of the `source` call, or any inner scope which can see it.

To improve modularity, we should strongly consider no exposing variables defined in "foo.nu" outside of the file, nor allowing "foo.nu" to variable capture any variables not defined in the file. In this proposed refactor, I assume this to be the case.

Instead, the goal of `source`-d files will be to provide commands and not variables. We will, however, still need to track the local variables and their bindings, so we can properly convert them to VarIds.

### `source` at evaluation time

During evaluation time, a new scope frame is created for the `source`-d file to run in. The evaluator will treat the `source`-d scope frame as another Block-Owned Scope Frame, evaluating the `source`-d file as if it were a frame that has no captures, no parent, and only local variables.

The resulting value from running this block will be returned, though it's unclear if this step is necessary.

## Conclusion

This refactor should help streamline the current use of variables, so that we no longer need to lock to read or write the variable values or command arguments. The changes to the parser allow far more scoping discipline, which should remove the current scope leaks. Finally, the use of interning should remove the need to do lookups during evaluation, as we already know where to look for the given definition.

These slots allow us to create local VarIds that are valid inside of the Block. These ids prevent having to lookup variable names in a scope. Instead, we would need only to use the VarId as an index into the vec held by the scope frame.

Parameters to blocks likewise will be given slots and held in the Block-Owned Scope Frame. To the Block, these parameters are just another variable during evaluation time. They just happen to be setup by the caller before the CapturedBlock gets evaluated.

Looking at an example:

```

let foo = {|y|
  let z = 10
  $x + $y + $z
}
do $foo 7
```

Once parsed, we have this pseudo-code:
```

```

The `foo` definition has a Block. This Block is turned into a BlockId during block interning (see above). When the `let foo = ...` line is run, we evaluate the Block expression, which gives us back a CapturedBlock value. This CapturedBlock contains the captured part of the frame we'll later use, along with the BlockId of the block to run.

```

  captures: [Value::int(3)]
  block_id: 1,
}
```

Next, when we run the block during `do $foo 7` we first setup the rest of the Block-Owned Scope Frame:

```
ScopeFrame {
  block: Box<CapturedBlock>
  vars: vec![],
}
```
The parameters are then pushed onto the vars, and we make space for the future vars:
```

  block: Box<CapturedBlock>
  vars: vec![Value::int(7), Var::empty],
}
```
(we may want to improve this further in the future, so we don't spend time on pushing the unused empty)

Finally, once we're running the block, as the `let z = 10` is finally run, we get our final:

```
  vars: vec![Value::int(7), Var::int(10)],
```

You'll notice that the captured variables are split from the local variables. This is to prevent having to do extra copying when a block is invoked. Instead, we check the VarId, and if it is larger than the number of captures, we look for the variable as a local.

**Note:** At this point, we should already know the DefIds for all CallInfo sites. We don't need to manage them in the Scope during evaluation. Instead, this should all be resolved during parse time, using the parse-time scope.

## Mutability

Block-Owned Stack Frames must be mutable by `run_block`. Without this, there's no way to set variables with their values. To allow for this, we need to ensure that variable declaration **are the only thing in the pipeline** so that we can detect it and properly convert the Arc to a mutable reference for updates. We can relax this restriction after some experience with it, but the initial restriction is what allows us to be safe to mutate during runtime.

## Global parts of scope

There are a few parts of global scope that we currently mutate, including state specific to directory-specific environments. We can leave this as part of scope or move it into a protected place inside of EvaluationContext. If these need to be mutable, they'll need to remain protected by locks. If these can be set during parse time and then are later read-only, we should be able to use an Arc instead.

## Aliases

The logic for Aliases can follow similarly to Definitions. During parse time, we should know in advance that a call site will bind to an alias. Even more, we can fully expand this alias during parse time so that we do not need to handle aliases during evaluation time.

Some care needs to be taken to ensure we can give proper error spans if an expanded alias later fails to evaluate.

## Entering and exiting scopes

Under the current system, we manually enter and exit scopes. This allows us more fine-grained control of when we want to use the current scope or to start with a fresh scope frame (and fall back to parents when doing lookup).

With the above changes, all of this logic changes. Calls always go through the Block-Owned Scope Frame logic detailed above. There is no longer a notion of entering and exiting scopes. This has one exception, the use of imports like `source`, which is detailed below.

## Handling `source`

The `source` command has multiple duties in the current system. During parse time, the `source` command will load in the definitions available in the `source`-d file and put them into scope. During evaluation time, `source` will run the block given at the top-level of the `source`-d file. Let us explore each of these:

```

```

Unexpected Behavior from `groupby_rolling` when using `by` parameter

**What language are you using?**

Python

**Have you tried latest version of polars?**

    [yes]

**What version of polars are you using?**

'0.13.49'

**What operating system are you using polars on?**

Windows 10

**What language version are you using**

python-3.9.6

**Describe your bug.**

I wanted to test `groupby_rolling` a try, using a test-dataframe where I could have used `groupy_dynamic` as well, but for the final use case, I would need `groupby_rolling`.

I create a dataframe with 20 records for each of 10 groups as follows
```python
import datetime
import itertools

import pandas as pd
import polars as pl

df = pd.DataFrame({
    'g': itertools.chain(*[[i] * 20 for i in range(10)]),
    'd': itertools.chain(*[[datetime.datetime(2020, 1, 1) + datetime.timedelta(days=i) for i in range(20)] for _ in range(10)]),
    'v': itertools.chain(*[list(range(20)) for _ in range(10)])
})
```
The resulting dataframe has
* 20 entries for every group (identified by the integer in column `g`)
* for each group has one entry from 2020-01-01 until 2020-01-20

I want to calculate the number of records per group in a rolling window defined by `d` and a fixed `period`. For this I proceeded as such:

```python
out = pl.DataFrame(df).sort(['d']).groupby_rolling(index_column='d', by='g', period="5d").agg([pl.count()])
```

**Expected behavior**

Dataframe with
* One record per group and day
* `count` is 1 for entries at 2020-01-01, 2 for entries at 2020-01-01, .... 5 for entries at 2020-01-05 and any higher date

**Actual Behavior**

* The result is as expected for values of `d` >= `2020-01-06` (every value of `d` appears once for every value of `g` and `count` is equal to 5).
* However, there are deviations for smaller values of `d`: Only one value of `d` appears per group, but five times, taking each value from 1 to 5 for `count`
  * For `g` = 0 or 1, I see `2020-01-01` 5 times.
  * For `g` = 2 or 3, I see `2020-01-02` 5 times
  * ...
  * For `g` = 8 or 9, I see `2020-01-05` 5 times

Bug in `groupby_rolling` for `offset` < `-period - 1` when using additional groupby columns

#### What language are you using?

**Python**

#### Which feature gates did you use?

This can be ignored by Python & JS users.

#### Have you tried latest version of polars?

- [yes] (0.13.51)

If the problem was resolved, please update polars. :)

#### What version of polars are you using?

0.13.51

#### What operating system are you using polars on?

Win10

#### What language version are you using
Python 3.9.6

#### Describe your bug.

When using `groupby_rolling`, the `offset` should specify the start of the rolling window relative to the value in the `index_column` (see [documentation](https://pola-rs.github.io/polars/py-polars/html/reference/api/polars.DataFrame.groupby_rolling.html?highlight=groupby_rolling#polars.DataFrame.groupby_rolling)).

When using additional groupby columns (parameter `by` specified), it appears that this is not working as expected.

* It appears that this is working as expected for values larger than or equal `-period` (the default).
* For `offset = -period - 1`, the result is not what I would have expected, but it might be intended.
* For `offset < -period - 1`, the result becomes unusable (several columns have only `null` values).

#### What are the steps to reproduce the behavior?

**Example**
(I am shamelessly re-using the excellent example provided by @cbilot in #3772 here)
```python
from datetime import datetime
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"group": pl.arange(0, 3, eager=True), }).join(
    pl.DataFrame(
        {
            "datetime": pl.date_range(
                datetime(2020, 1, 1), datetime(2020, 1, 5), "1d"
            ),
        }
    ),
    how="cross",
)
df
```

Result:
```
group | datetime
-- | --
i64 | datetime[ns]
0 | 2020-01-01 00:00:00
0 | 2020-01-02 00:00:00
0 | 2020-01-03 00:00:00
0 | 2020-01-04 00:00:00
0 | 2020-01-05 00:00:00
1 | 2020-01-01 00:00:00
1 | 2020-01-02 00:00:00
1 | 2020-01-03 00:00:00
1 | 2020-01-04 00:00:00
1 | 2020-01-05 00:00:00
2 | 2020-01-01 00:00:00
2 | 2020-01-02 00:00:00
2 | 2020-01-03 00:00:00
2 | 2020-01-04 00:00:00
2 | 2020-01-05 00:00:00
```

Now running groupby operation
```python
(
    df.
    groupby_rolling(index_column='datetime', by='group', period='2d', offset='-4d').
    agg([pl.count().alias('count')]).
    head()
)
```

(Note that `offset` is less than "-period - 1" (day)).

#### What is the actual behavior?
```
group | datetime | count
-- | -- | --
i64 | datetime[ns] | u32
null | 2020-01-01 00:00:00 | 0
null | 2020-01-02 00:00:00 | 0
null | 2020-01-03 00:00:00 | 0
null | 2020-01-04 00:00:00 | 0
null | 2020-01-05 00:00:00 | 0
```

#### What is the expected behavior?

I would expect a valid entry (column `group` set to non-null value, column `count` set to a value of `> 0` at least for `datetime` entries larger than or equal `2020-01-04`.

null | 2020-01-05 00:00:00 | 0
```

I would expect a valid entry (column `group` set to non-null value, column `count` set to a value of `> 0` at least for `datetime` entries larger than or equal `2020-01-04`.

raw_text:
Deep equality of pl.Expr trees

#### Describe your feature request

`pl.Expr`s supply a wide array of operator overloads including `__eq__` which is great syntactic sugar to construct more complicated nested predicate expressions. However, by losing `__eq__` we no longer have a way to recursively check that `pl.Expr`s indeed are equal to each other. Semantically:

```
pl.lit(3) == pl.lit(5)
```

is a boolean expression. I would like something like a `.equals()`:

```
pl.lit(3).equals(pl.lit(5))
```

which is a boolean value in python. Here, it would be `False` because `pl.lit(3)` is an expression node with a value of 3 as its member while `pl.lit(5)` is an expression node with a value of 5 as its member. One can imagine more complicated expressions:

```
(pl.lit(3) + pl.lit(5)).equals(pl.lit(3) + (pl.lit(1) + pl.lit(4)))
```

Would yield `False` although the boolean expression would evaluate to true, since LHS looks like:

```
add
├─ pl.lit(3)
├─ pl.lit(5)
```

And RHS looks like:

```
add
├─ pl.lit(3)
├─ add # This node is different!
       ├─ pl.lit(1)
       ├─ pl.lit(4)
```

This would be really helpful if we want applications to build upon polars, since those applications should have tests to verify correctness of the polars expressions created underneath.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

This repro below is the result of a binary-search curated large data set stripped down to 1 value column and the smallest window I can repro the error with. target_text:
groupby_dynamic creates duplicate rows under certain datetime gaps

### Polars version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Issue description

This repro below is the result of a binary-search curated large data set stripped down to 1 value column and the smallest window I can repro the error with. It's important to note that when the value column isn't zero, the extra entries _actually don't agree in aggregation value_, which is bizarre. Perhaps it's because the ts associated with the window is labeled incorrectly?

#### What language are you using?

**Python**

#### What version of polars are you using?

0.13.22

#### What operating system are you using polars on?

Ubuntu 20.04

#### What language version are you using

python 3.10.04

#### Describe your bug.

Sub-process gets stucked when parent process uses reading feature of polars (e.g. read_parquet, scan_parquet)

#### What are the steps to reproduce the behavior?

```python
import multiprocessing

import polars as pl


def test_sub_process(data: pl.DataFrame):
    xdata = data.lazy().filter(pl.col('a') > 0).collect()
    print("Filtered")


test_df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "a": [0, 2, 3, 4, 5],
        "b": [0, 4, 5, 56, 4]
    }
)
test_df.write_parquet("/tmp/test.parquet")
test_df = pl.scan_parquet(
    "/tmp/test.parquet",
).collect()
proc = multiprocessing.Process(target=test_sub_process,
                               args=(
                                   test_df,
                               ))
proc.start()
proc.join()
print("Executed sub process")
```

#### What is the actual behavior?

Sub-process gets stucked and never return to python code

#### What is the expected behavior?

Printed out messages

LazyFrame/planner error with `explode => filter` combination

### Polars version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Issue description

LazyFrame differs from DataFrame for sequenced `explode` and `filter` ops.

### Reproducible example

Minimised test-case, showing expected progression of the explode/filter ops at each stage.

_Setup:_
```python
import polars as pl

df = pl.from_dict({
  'i': [[0, 1], [1, 2]],
  'n': [0, None],
})
# ┌───────────┬──────┐
# │ i         ┆ n    │
# │ ---       ┆ ---  │
# │ list[i64] ┆ i64  │
# ╞═══════════╪══════╡
# │ [0, 1]    ┆ 0    │
# │ [1, 2]    ┆ null │
# └───────────┴──────┘

def explode_filter( frame ):
  return (
    frame
      .explode( 'i' ) 
      # ┌─────┬──────┐
      # │ i   ┆ n    │
      # │ --- ┆ ---  │
      # │ i64 ┆ i64  │
      # ╞═════╪══════╡
      # │ 0   ┆ 0    │
      # │ 1   ┆ 0    │
      # │ 1   ┆ null │
      # │ 2   ┆ null │
      # └─────┴──────┘
      .filter( pl.col('n').count().over( ['i'] ) == 2 )
      # ┌─────┬──────┐
      # │ i   ┆ n    │
      # │ --- ┆ ---  │
      # │ i64 ┆ i64  │
      # ╞═════╪══════╡
      # │ 1   ┆ 0    │
      # │ 1   ┆ null │
      # └─────┴──────┘
      .filter( pl.col('n').is_not_null() )
      # ┌─────┬─────┐
      # │ i   ┆ n   │
      # │ --- ┆ --- │
      # │ i64 ┆ i64 │
      # ╞═════╪═════╡
      # │ 1   ┆ 0   │
      # └─────┴─────┘
  )
```
_Different results:_
```python
explode_filter( df )
# ┌─────┬─────┐
# │ i   ┆ n   │
# │ --- ┆ --- │
# │ i64 ┆ i64 │
# ╞═════╪═════╡
# │ 1   ┆ 0   │   << expected result
# └─────┴─────┘

explode_filter( df.lazy() ).collect()
# ┌─────┬─────┐
# │ i   ┆ n   │
# │ --- ┆ --- │
# │ i64 ┆ i64 │
# ╞═════╪═════╡
# └─────┴─────┘   << no values
```

### Expected behavior

DataFrame vs LazyFrame execution should have the same result.

Type Checking Expression [Python]

### Problem description

I want to be able to test column types via polars expressions, so that I don't need to apply a python function. Say, I have a series of an unknown type. This could be a date column, that is sometimes linux timestamp ints, date string, or just a pl.Dates, I can't currently test it via polars without doing row-wise checks.

What I'd like to be able to do
```
(
  pl.when(pl.col("date").is_type(str))
 .then(pl.col("date").str.strptime(pl.Date, fmt="%Y-%m-%d"))
 .when(pl.col("date").is_type(int))
 .then(pl.from_epoch(pl.col("date"), unit="ms"))
 .otherwise(pl.col("date").cast(pl.Date))
)
 ```
 
 Currently I have to do something like this:
  ```
 def cast_dates(x):
        # isoformat date string
        if isinstance(x, str):
            return datetime.strptime(x, '%Y-%m-%d').date()
            return x.str.strptime(pl.Date, fmt="%Y-%m-%d")

        # linux timestamp
        if isinstance(x, int):
            return datetime.fromtimestamp(x / 1000).date()
            pl.from_epoch(x, unit="ms")

        return date(x)
 
 ...
   
  pl.col("date").apply(cast_dates)
  
 ```
 

 I don't know if this is possible (or feasible), but it would help a lot with casting, especially as I'm importing from json.

Feature Request: option to scroll in reverse

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I frequently need to get the last N entries which match a filter

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Being able to start at an ID and scroll backwards would be convenient and more efficient.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
What I currently do is purposely choose a higher limit than I want (say 50 when I really want 10) and start at Last_ID - 50. If I get >=10 results I keep the last 10, otherwise I have to repeat the query until I get how many I want. I can't predict beforehand how many IDs my filter will reject.

**Additional context**
I know this is veering into not-a-vector-db-feature territory, but scroll already exists and this would make it quite a bit more useful, imo

**Related**
- https://github.com/orgs/qdrant/discussions/6469

raw_text:
ContextQuery with Manhattan distance changes exact Top-k order after uniform positive scaling

## Current Behavior

When using `ContextQuery` with `Distance.MANHATTAN`, multiplying all stored vectors and all context positive/negative vectors by the same positive constant, such as `0.5`, changes the exact Top-k order.

This is not caused by ties or approximate search. The reproduction uses `search_params = exact=True`, and the reordered points have clear score gaps.

Actual output:

```text
base = [
  (3, -0.9085107445716858),
  (7, -0.9358134269714355),
  (2, -0.938614010810852),
  (6, -1.0794621706008911),
  (5, -1.268345832824707),
  (0, -1.2774608135223389),
  (4, -1.3616465330123901),
  (1, -1.3720533847808838)
]

scaled = [
  (3, -0.5949209332466125),
  (6, -0.775405764579773),
  (7, -0.8793697357177734),
  (2, -0.8843286037445068),
  (5, -1.0397822856903076),
  (4, -1.049561619758606),
  (0, -1.0548453330993652),
  (1, -1.0636745691299438)
]
```

Order comparison:

```text
base ids   = [3, 7, 2, 6, 5, 0, 4, 1]
scaled ids = [3, 6, 7, 2, 5, 4, 0, 1]
```

For example, `id=6` moves from rank 4 to rank 2. `id=7` and `id=2` move down, and `id=4` and `id=0` also swap order.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Qdrant `1.17.1` and connect via gRPC at `localhost:6334`.

2. Create a 2-dimensional collection using Manhattan distance.

3. Insert the following 8 vectors and run a `ContextQuery` with two positive/negative context pairs.

4. Run the query twice: once with the original data, and once after multiplying all stored vectors and all context positive/negative vectors by `0.5`.

```python
from qdrant_client import QdrantClient, models
from qdrant_client.models import Distance, VectorParams, PointStruct

client = QdrantClient(host="localhost", grpc_port=6334, prefer_grpc=True)

BASE = "mr_context_scale_base"
SCALED = "mr_context_scale_scaled"
SCALE = 0.5

pairs = [
    ([-6.9126648832641, -9.028747637394439], [0.1560544722562902, -0.8071061306133345]),
    ([6.681069376098151, -4.255406538874304], [5.6895384366986, -4.652053059779284]),
]

vectors = {
    0: [-2.7554312531122305, 7.471520205336269],
    1: [1.484137139862245, -6.5624267135932834],
    2: [8.486627126148662, 3.020608441705246],
    3: [-9.982520521061748, 4.848763468064597],
    4: [0.47597175386690616, -6.675670490096321],
    5: [-3.211249569996517, 8.903103227051371],
    6: [-4.332591299218644, -2.7602545490341406],
    7: [8.370447508336397, -1.162496642761603],
}

def recreate(name):
    try:
        client.delete_collection(name)
    except Exception:
        pass

    client.create_collection(
        collection_name=name,
        vectors_config=VectorParams(size=2, distance=Distance.MANHATTAN),
    )

def run(name, scale):
    recreate(name)

    client.upsert(
        collection_name=name,
        points=[
            PointStruct(id=i, vector=[x * scale for x in v])
            for i, v in vectors.items()
        ],
        wait=True,
    )

    context = [
        models.ContextPair(
            positive=[x * scale for x in p],
            negative=[x * scale for x in n],
        )
        for p, n in pairs
    ]

    points = client.query_points(
        collection_name=name,
        query=models.ContextQuery(context=context),
        limit=8,
        search_params=models.SearchParams(exact=True),
        with_payload=False,
        with_vectors=False,
    ).points

    return [(p.id, p.score) for p in points]

base = run(BASE, 1.0)
scaled = run(SCALED, SCALE)

print("base =", base)
print("scaled =", scaled)

print("base ids   =", [x[0] for x in base])
print("scaled ids =", [x[0] for x in scaled])

if [x[0] for x in base] != [x[0] for x in scaled]:
    print("BUG REPRODUCED")
```

## Expected Behavior

For Manhattan distance, uniformly multiplying all stored vectors and all query/context vectors by the same positive constant should preserve the Top-k order.

Manhattan distance is positively homogeneous:

```text
d(c * x, c * y) = c * d(x, y), where c > 0
```

Therefore, the distance differences induced by each positive/negative context pair should only be scaled by a positive constant. The absolute scores may change, but the exact Top-k order should remain unchanged.

The expected order should remain:

```text
[3, 7, 2, 6, 5, 0, 4, 1]
```

## Possible Solution

The issue may come from the current per-pair loss aggregation in `ContextQuery`.

The implementation appears to apply a nonlinear `fast_sigmoid()` transformation independently to each context-pair margin before summing the losses. The logic is similar to:

```rust
let difference = positive - negative - MARGIN;
fast_sigmoid(ScoreType::min(difference, 0.0))
```

Then the per-pair losses are summed.

This breaks positive scaling invariance. Although `fast_sigmoid()` is monotonic for a single input,

```text
sum(fast_sigmoid(c * diff_i))
```

does not necessarily preserve the same ranking as:

```text
sum(fast_sigmoid(diff_i))
```

A possible fix is to avoid applying the nonlinear squashing function independently to each pair before aggregation. For example, the implementation could aggregate raw margins first and then apply normalization or a nonlinear transformation once, or use another aggregation method that preserves ranking under uniform positive scaling for Manhattan distance.

## Context (Environment)

This affects the predictability of context search. With Manhattan distance, uniformly changing the vector scale or unit should not change exact Top-k results.

Environment:

```text
Qdrant version = 1.17.1
Connection = localhost:6334 gRPC
search_params = exact=True
metric = Distance.MANHATTAN
scale = 0.5
```

This makes context search sensitive to vector scale. Two semantically equivalent datasets that differ only by a uniform positive scaling factor can return different exact rankings.

## Detailed Description

The issue appears when `ContextQuery` uses multiple positive/negative context pairs.

For Manhattan distance, if all stored vectors, positive vectors, and negative vectors are multiplied by the same positive constant, all Manhattan distances are multiplied by that constant. The underlying geometric relationship between candidates is unchanged.

However, the current context scoring path appears to apply `fast_sigmoid()` independently to each pair margin and then sum the transformed losses. Since `fast_sigmoid()` is nonlinear, applying it per pair changes the relative contribution of different context pairs after scaling. As a result, the final score order can change even though the query and dataset are geometrically equivalent up to a positive scale factor.

This reproduction uses ordinary 2D vectors. It does not rely on extremely large or small values. It also does not rely on approximate search, since `exact=True` is used. Therefore, this looks like a deterministic scoring issue rather than numerical instability or ANN behavior.

## Possible Implementation

Possible implementation directions:

1. Add a metamorphic test for `ContextQuery` with Manhattan distance.  
   Multiply all stored vectors and all context vectors by the same positive constant and verify that exact Top-k IDs remain unchanged.

2. Inspect the location of the per-pair `fast_sigmoid()` call in `ContextPair::loss_by`.

Investigate Multivalue Fastfield indexing regression 

Previously we passed typed iterators into the construction, which were used for serializing the data. The random access `Column` trait was only used for estimation.

Now we pass `Column` for both, which only has `Box<Iterator>`. The `get_val` alternative is slower and is used currently in the line train method. 

Strongly typed iterators on the type are currently impossible, due limitations on `impl Trait` (maybe resolved in next stable rust with GAT, or more [return_position_impl_trait_in_trait](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/labels/F-return_position_impl_trait_in_trait), Update: That's the correct tracking issue https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/63063)

Notifying Quinn about network path changes

Sometimes the application knows about network path changes that Quinn may not detect immediately to.  If the network changed significantly it can often be faster to reach optimal throughput and latency again by resetting things like the congestion controller, rtt estimator and mtu detection to initial states.

This was explored a bit in #1842 but that was ultimately closed.  However this topic was recently brought up again in another issue and there was an indication that something like this could belong in Quinn.  So this is an attempt to find out if we can get any closer to that.

It seems the biggest difference in thinking is whether this should be per `Connection` or for the entire `Endpoint`.
* The motivation for per-connection is that these details are stored per-connection since each connection has its own network path.
* While for the entire endpoint the argument is that an endpoint only has a single socket and this is probably the most common way for an application to know the network path changed.

Perhaps it is easier to agree on what the API and implementation in quinn-proto should be, because there an API on the `Connection` seems better suited.  Currently we have https://github.com/n0-computer/quinn/blob/02f3b33de039951bfaf4cc383d9f0ec6cdf8dcb1/quinn-proto/src/connection/mod.rs#L1317 as the entrypoint to this in the fork for iroh.  The [implementation](https://github.com/n0-computer/quinn/blob/02f3b33de039951bfaf4cc383d9f0ec6cdf8dcb1/quinn-proto/src/connection/paths.rs#L121) currently does 3 things:

- Creates a new `RttEstimator` from the original `TransportConfig` settings.
- Creates a new congestion controller from the original `TransportConfig` settings.
- [Resets the MTU discovery](https://github.com/n0-computer/quinn/blob/02f3b33de039951bfaf4cc383d9f0ec6cdf8dcb1/quinn-proto/src/connection/mtud.rs#L59), essentially re-creating a new one with the same settings it was originally created with.

What is the opinion on adding this in some form to quinn-proto?

Question about scheduling of maps over containers of known length

I read the FAQ and looked through the docs and couldn't find an answer to this but maybe I'm using the wrong search terms.

Say I have something like a Vec or a slice where we can `O(1)` query its length. If I do `slice.par_iter().map(|x| { ... })` and we ignore work stealing for the moment (assume every thread takes identical amount of time per element and the number of threads evenly divides the the number of elements to process), does each thread get a contiguous chunk of size `slice.len()/N` pushed on to its queue, or is each individual slice element round robinned across all threads? Two reasons I ask:

* For cache locality and prefetch, it's better for a thread to repeatedly handle elements close together in memory, ideally linearly.
* In my use case the items being iterated are keys used to query a thread local data structure, where often querying with `slice[i]` involves it internally loading and caching the data for `slice[i+1]`, so if the same thread subsequently does the query for `slice[i+1]` I will hit the cache.

This can't be done in all cases, because if what's feeding `map` is an opaque stream of values you don't have any idea up front how many elements are coming down the pipe, but for Vec/slice should be possible. I see there's a `Split` trait, but I'm not sure if that's intended for helping users manually force this kind of thing or if out of the box it's even necessary if the scheduling does this already. From the POV of my code it thinks it's only operating on one element at a time even though the thread local data structure internally loads query result for `slice[i+1]`, so using `chunks` feels artificial but maybe that's how I should guarantee this?

P.S. thanks for the sweet library :+1:

Cyclic package dependency with certain package features set

Create a simple cargo project with these dependencies in Cargo.toml

```
parking_lot = { version = "0.12.3", features = ["deadlock_detection"] }
once_cell = { version = "1.19.0", features = ["parking_lot"] }
cc = { version = "1.1.0", features = ["parallel"] }
```

Run `cargo check`, then cargo will emits error:
```
error: cyclic package dependency: package `backtrace v0.3.73` depends on itself. Cycle:
package `backtrace v0.3.73`
    ... which satisfies dependency `backtrace = "^0.3.60"` of package `parking_lot_core v0.9.10`
    ... which satisfies dependency `parking_lot_core = "^0.9.3"` of package `once_cell v1.19.0`
    ... which satisfies dependency `once_cell = "^1.19"` of package `cc v1.1.0`
    ... which satisfies dependency `cc = "^1.0.97"` of package `backtrace v0.3.73`
```

The dependencies formed a cycle after https://github.com/rust-lang/cc-rs/pull/1037 (which introduces the `once_cell` dependency)

raw_text:
Improve tag creation tracking note

I've been looking at a number of Miri errors recently where tracking the relevant tag results in just two messages like the following:
```
test join ... note: tracking was triggered
  --> /home/ben/futures-rs/futures-task/src/waker_ref.rs:58:16
   |
58 |     let ptr = (&**wake as *const W) as *const ();
   |                ^^^^^^^ created tag 199076
   |
```
```
   --> /home/ben/.rustup/toolchains/nightly-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lib/rustlib/src/rust/library/core/src/ptr/non_null.rs:327:18
    |
327 |         unsafe { &*self.as_ptr() }
    |                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ trying to reborrow for SharedReadWrite at alloc74291, but parent tag <199076> does not have an appropriate item in the borrow stack
    |
```
I suspect that in this case the problem is that the created borrow is SRO for an SRW use, or an SRW tag for a Unique use. It would be good if Miri explained a bit more about the tag.

I'd be submitting the PR to do this, but the diagnostic code is a bit displaced from the information about the tag, so improving this requires a bit more finesse with the code than I have patience for today.

ctpop intrinsics shouldn't be unsafe

```

raw_text:
Possible improvement in runtime efficiency of generated `libloading` wrapper type impl

[`libloading`'s docs for the `get` method](https://docs.rs/libloading/0.6.5/libloading/struct.Library.html#method.get) mention the following:

> The symbol may not contain any null bytes, with an exception of last byte. A null terminated symbol may avoid a string allocation in some cases.

This implies that passing a null-terminated symbol is recommended.

However, bindgen [currently doesn't generate](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-bindgen/blob/master/tests/expectations/tests/dynamic_loading_template.rs#L23-L24) null-terminated symbols:

```rust
        let foo = __library.get("foo".as_bytes()).map(|sym| *sym);
        let foo1 = __library.get("foo1".as_bytes()).map(|sym| *sym);
```

    records
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(index, record)| (key_fn(record), index))
        .collect()
}
```

Query Z-order / window level

Hi, I have a use case for knowing the Z ordering of all visible windows.  I searched through the issues and PRs, and I think that #2534 and #1883 are almost what I'm looking for, except that they don't have a way of querying what the current Z order is.  Is it possible/easy/reasonable to add a new `WindowEvent` variant that reports the window's current on-screen order?  Something like `ZOrderChanged(i64)`?  The value of the number is the ordering depth, with 0 being the front-most ('closest' to the camera).  Negative values aren't allowed, but if there are platforms that don't use unsigned integers for this request, they still need to be able to be supported.  Note that there will have to be a way of directly asking a window what its Z order is, so that users don't have to keep track of that information themselves, or force it in some manner (`current_z_order(&self) -> Result<i64, NotSupportedError>` would be my choice).

warning: `...` range patterns are deprecated

- Rocket version: 0.4.1
- Rust version: rustc 1.37.0-nightly (b25ee6449 2019-06-17)
- OS: Ubuntu 18.04

Compiling this code:

```rust
#![feature(proc_macro_hygiene, decl_macro)]

#[macro_use] extern crate rocket;

#[get("/route")]
fn route() {
    match 1 {
        0..=24 => {},
        _ => {}
    }
}

fn main() {}
```

results in this warning:

```
warning: `...` range patterns are deprecated
 --> src/main.rs:8:10
  |
8 |         0..=24 => {},
  |          ^^^ help: use `..=` for an inclusive range
  |
  = note: #[warn(ellipsis_inclusive_range_patterns)] on by default
```

which is unexpected, given that the `..=` syntax is used in the code.

Removing the `get` attribute stops the warning from being emitted.

#![feature(proc_macro_hygiene, decl_macro)]

Cookie "SameSite" value set to "None" is actually "Lax"


In the Cookie struct, regarding [the function set_same_site](https://api.rocket.rs/v0.4/rocket/http/struct.Cookie.html#method.set_same_site):
When the parameter is set to SameSite::None, the attribute SameSite is not set, but in most recent browser (since chrome version 76+) when this value is unset the default one is SameSite::Lax, so there is no way to set it to the actual "None" value.

It would be helpful to have this fix.

raw_text:
Limits in Rocket.toml not working

**Description**

I was trying to config some limits in the Rocket.toml like:
```
[global.limits]
json = 104857600
bytes = 104857600
"PhactoryAPI.DispatchBlocks" = 104857600
```
Found it doesn't work.

It is because that rocket deserializes the Limits from a Figment with `figment::util::vec_tuple_map`:

https://github.com/SergioBenitez/Rocket/blob/f64029f079882c1fe8e47d65d4a57ec260729bea/core/lib/src/data/limits.rs#L125

And later trying to binary search the enties in the limits would fail because the deserialized limits are unsorted .

[Feature] Ability to serialize cookie to json

I would like to request ability to serialize cookie to json. And I can even PR if maintainer is interested in adding it.

The plan is basically to edit a new Cookie type having similar fields to Cookie crate (because cookie crate Cookie type fields are private etc so hard to add serialization support using serde). Implement serde derive and implement From trait. 

I think this shouldnt be issue with backward compatibility as request uses it own Cookie type anyway?

### Usecase.

Sometime we need to debug whether we are sending request properly and retrieving cookie and many browser extension export import cookie in json format . This should really help to debug such issues.

After implementing we shall be able to get cookie in json format like this

```json
[
  {
    "name": "cookie_name",
    "value": "cookie_value",
    "expires": "0020-10-20 19:31:35 +0",
    "max_age": null,
    "domain": "google.com",
    "path": "/",
    "secure": null,
    "http_only": true,
    "same_site": "Lax"
  },
...
]
```

raw_text:
[Feature proposal] Dynamic signing of TLS connection

# The actual need

Let's say we have a hardware token like a [HSM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardware_security_module), a [Yubikey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YubiKey) or any [security token](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_token) compatible with [PKCS#11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PKCS_11).

We could imagine using the key/certificate pair stored in the security token to secure the TLS connection. That way, on the other side of the connection, we are sure that we are talking to someone who has that unique security token.

# The problem

The private key **cannot** be extracted from the security token (that's the whole purpose) so we can't give it to `reqwest`.

# The solution

When creating a TLS connection, data needs to be signed by the security token. This means that, instead of giving a [private key as an identity](https://docs.rs/reqwest/latest/reqwest/tls/struct.Identity.html), we need to give a function that will sign the data. On step further would be to also allow a dynamic certificate.

The good news is that [`rustls` already have this feature](https://docs.rs/rustls/latest/rustls/struct.ConfigBuilder.html#method.with_client_cert_resolver). 
However, as you stated in #2569 and #605, exposing `rustls` API means risking breaking changes on a simple update.
A wrapper would do the trick but it doesn't seems that `native_tls` would support that feature.

Would having a feature for `rustls` only but without exposing `rustls` API be acceptable for you ?

Requests timeout when making a large number

Hello,

I'm having issues with requests timing out. I'm parsing a CSV file that contains a large number of sites (10,000) and buffering (1000) records at a time and making requests to the sites. Each site is different and the maximum number of futures at any one time is under my OS's maximum allowed number of open files. 
```
$ ulimit -a
core file size          (blocks, -c) 0
data seg size           (kbytes, -d) unlimited
scheduling priority             (-e) 0
file size               (blocks, -f) unlimited
pending signals                 (-i) 62386
max locked memory       (kbytes, -l) 16384
max memory size         (kbytes, -m) unlimited
open files                      (-n) 1024
pipe size            (512 bytes, -p) 8
POSIX message queues     (bytes, -q) 819200
real-time priority              (-r) 0
stack size              (kbytes, -s) 8192
cpu time               (seconds, -t) unlimited
max user processes              (-u) 62386
virtual memory          (kbytes, -v) unlimited
file locks                      (-x) unlimited
```

For a given run of the program:
```
$ ls /proc/28799/fd/ | wc -l
909
```


The code is done as follows:

```
        let fetches = csv_rx
            .take(10000)
            .map(|data| tokio::spawn(Agent::run(data, ctx.clone())))
            .buffer_unordered(1000)
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
```

In another part, I'm listening for these requests and then spawning a thread to handle it:
```
      while let Some(req) = rx.recv().await {
            let fut = HostResolver::do_request(req, client.clone(), request_timeout);
            let _ = tokio::spawn(fut);
        }
```

The client is initialised as:
```
        let client = ClientBuilder::new()
            .connection_verbose(true)
            .timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))
            .build()
            .unwrap();
```

And each request is created as:
```
            let mut headers = HeaderMap::new();

            headers.insert(DNT, HeaderValue::from(1));
            headers.insert(UPGRADE_INSECURE_REQUESTS, HeaderValue::from(1));
            headers.insert(
                USER_AGENT,
                HeaderValue::from_str(
                    "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT x.y; Win64; x64; rv:10.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/10.0",
                )
                .unwrap(),
            );
            headers.insert(ACCEPT, HeaderValue::from_str("text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,image/webp,image/apng,*/*;q=0.8,application/signed-exchange;v=b3;q=0.9").unwrap());
            headers.insert(
                ACCEPT_LANGUAGE,
                HeaderValue::from_str("en-GB,en-US;q=0.9,en;q=0.8").unwrap(),
            );
            headers.insert(
                ACCEPT_ENCODING,
                HeaderValue::from_str("deflate, gzip").unwrap(),
            );

            let req = client
                .get(&uri.to_string())
                .headers(headers)
                .body(Body::from(String::new()))
                .build()
                .unwrap();

            let req = client.execute(req);
```

The problem that I'm having is that after a certain number of requests/time has passed, most of the requests start to fail and timeout:
```
error sending request for url (****): operation timed out
```
I've tried this is many different ways and with both Hyper and Reqwest and I'm a bit lost as to what the problem is. I've tried increasing the number of Tokio threads and creating a new Client instance for each request or after X requests have been made. The websites are all different host addresses and will work fine from a browser when the application is running.

Would anyone be able to provide any guidance?

Thanks!

raw_text:
Skip Empty 'impl' Block Generation in 'sea-orm-cli generate entity' Command

I propose the addition of a flag to the CLI command sea-orm-cli generate entity that allows for skipping the generation of an empty impl block, specifically impl ActiveModelBehavior for ActiveModel {}.

```
sea-orm-cli generate entity --skip-generate-active-block_behaivior [list of tables]
```

For instance, when I intend to hash a user's password before inserting a new record, I would like to use the before_save implementation. Currently, this involves the following steps:

1. Adding the necessary logic directly to the generated file. However, this code gets deleted when the generate entity command is rerun.

2. Attempting to place the before_save logic in a different location but getting compilation error: "conflicting implementation" error.

The proposed flag would streamline this process and prevent the deletion of custom code during regeneration.

type "schema.x_enum" does not exist - after updating to SQLX 0.8.5

## Description

Before, to have an enum in a namespace that is not public, I would do the following:
```
#[derive(
    Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, EnumIter, DeriveActiveEnum, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema,
)]
#[sea_orm(
    rs_type = "String",
    db_type = "Enum",
    enum_name = "SCHEMA.X_ENUM"
)]
pub enum XEnum {
    #[sea_orm(string_value = "A")]
    A,
    #[sea_orm(string_value = "B")]
    B,
}

impl IntoActiveValue<Self> for XEnum {
    fn into_active_value(self) -> sea_orm::ActiveValue<Self> {
        sea_orm::ActiveValue::Set(self.clone())
    }
}
```
This was hacky but it would work fine. It seems that now, after updating to sqlx 0.8.5. This breaks and returns the error type "schema.x_enum" does not exist. 



## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an enum in a separate schema
2. Try to query it

### Expected Behavior

It's queriable

### Actual Behavior

Type doesn't exist

### Reproduces How Often

Yes

### Workarounds

I was able to work around it for now but setting the search_path to the schema, however, I am concerned about duplicate types if it ever shows up.

Issues with tables that do not have primary/unique keys

Hi!

When creating a table that does not have a primary key attached

## 1) Not able to create table that do not has primary key

Workarounds in https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm/issues/485 do not work. Using a unique col instead does also not work in my use case with pg_partman (`Execution Error: error returned from database: unique constraint on partitioned table must include all partitioning columns`).

Motivation: I am trying to make use of https://github.com/pgpartman/pg_partman/blob/master/doc/pg_partman_howto.md#simple-time-based-1-partition-per-day which wants me to create a parent table without having a primary key.

## 2) Compile errors with misleading error messages

Expected behavior: 

```rust
5  | #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, Eq)]
   |                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the trait `sea_orm::IdenStatic` is not implemented for `entities::table_without_primary_key::PrimaryKey`
```

Actual behavior:

I am getting misleading error messages for tables that have primary keys and were not modified.

```rust
5  | #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DeriveEntityModel, Eq)]
   |                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the trait `sea_orm::IdenStatic` is not implemented for `entities::table_with_primary_key::PrimaryKey`
```

I found that seaorm cli for does not add  `#[sea_orm(primary_key)]` to all tables when one of the tables is lacking of a primary key.

raw_text:
`sea-orm-cli` installation always fails with `'?' couldn't convert the error: 'regex::Error: std::error::Error' is not satisfied`

## Description

Installation of the `sea-orm-cli` fails both locally from gh repo and with `cargo install`. Same for all the crates that depend on the `sea-orm-cli` crate.

```
> cargo version
< cargo 1.89.0 (c24e10642 2025-06-23)

> rustup show
< Default host: aarch64-apple-darwin
```

## Steps to Reproduce
Run `cargo install sea-orm-cli`. Or in the `sea-orm` crate run `cargo install --path=sea-orm-cli`

### Expected Behavior
No compilation error

### Actual Behavior
```
error[E0277]: `?` couldn't convert the error: `regex::Error: std::error::Error` is not satisfied
   --> /sea-orm/sea-orm-cli/src/commands/migrate.rs:228:69
    |
212 | fn update_migrator(migration_name: &str, migration_dir: &str) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    |                                                                  -------------------------- required `regex::Error: std::error::Error` because of this
...
228 |     let mod_regex = Regex::new(r"mod\s+(?P<name>m\d{8}_\d{6}_\w+);")?;
    |                     ------------------------------------------------^ the trait `std::error::Error` is not implemented for `regex::Error`
    |                     |
    |                     this has type `Result<_, regex::Error>`
    |
    = note: the question mark operation (`?`) implicitly performs a conversion on the error value using the `From` trait
    = note: required for `Box<dyn std::error::Error>` to implement `From<regex::Error>`

error[E0277]: `?` couldn't convert the error: `regex::Error: std::error::Error` is not satisfied
   --> /sea-orm/sea-orm-cli/src/commands/migrate.rs:250:53
    |
212 | fn update_migrator(migration_name: &str, migration_dir: &str) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
    |                                                                  -------------------------- required `regex::Error: std::error::Error` because of this
...
250 |     let vec_regex = Regex::new(r"vec!\[[\s\S]+\]\n")?;
    |                     --------------------------------^ the trait `std::error::Error` is not implemented for `regex::Error`
    |                     |
    |                     this has type `Result<_, regex::Error>`
    |
    = note: the question mark operation (`?`) implicitly performs a conversion on the error value using the `From` trait
    = note: required for `Box<dyn std::error::Error>` to implement `From<regex::Error>`

For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0277`.
error: could not compile `sea-orm-cli` (lib) due to 2 previous errors
warning: build failed, waiting for other jobs to finish...
```

### Reproduces How Often
Always

### Workarounds
1. If I use `--locked` when installing with `cargo install sea-orm-cli` - no error occurs
2. However, after such installation the resulting behavior of the generated crates is unexpected. For example:

```
> cargo install sea-orm-cli --locked
# say installed successfully

> sea-orm-cli migrate init
> cd migration
> cargo build
```
After the `cargo build` I face the same error with `couldn't convert the error: regex::Error: std::error::Error is not satisfied`.

After some experiments, I found out that switching to `std` for `regex`, i.e. by removing `default-features = false` in `sear-orm-cli/Cargo.toml` fixes an error. 

Also if I define `regex` as a dependency in my own crate where the same `sea-orm-migration` is defined as dependency too (say in `migration` crate generated after calling `sea-orm-cli migrate init`), then everything builds fine without errors. Seems `cargo` chooses most suitable version the one which has `std`. Here's an example:
```toml
[package]
name = "migration"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
publish = false

[lib]
name = "migration"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[dependencies]
tokio = { version = "1.47.1", features = ["full"] }
regex = "1" # that fixes everything

[dependencies.sea-orm-migration]
version = "1.0.0"
features = [
  # Enable at least one `ASYNC_RUNTIME` and `DATABASE_DRIVER` feature if you want to run migration via CLI.
  # View the list of supported features at https://www.sea-ql.org/SeaORM/docs/install-and-config/database-and-async-runtime.
  # e.g.
  "runtime-tokio-rustls", # `ASYNC_RUNTIME` feature
  "sqlx-sqlite",
]

```

## Versions
sea-orm - 1.1.14
sea-orm-cli - 1.1.14
sea-orm-migration - 1.1.14

I could imagine an annotation on the entity column telling SeaORM not to log values for that column.

sea-orm-cli generates invalid belongs_to when `--tables` specified

## Description

 When generating entities with SeaORM CLI v2 (rc) using `--tables` to restrict output to a subset of tables, the generator still emits relations that reference tables outside the selected set. In modularized projects, this produces code that refers to `super::<other_table>::Entity` which is not present in the module, causing compilation failures.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. create tables with this SQL

```sql
create table parent ( id serial not null );
create table child ( id serial not null, parent_id int references parent(id) );
```

2. `sea-orm-cli generate entity` with specify `--tables parent`

### Expected Behavior

under `Relation` enum  `#[sea_orm(belongs_to ...)]` filtered with `--tables`.

### Actual Behavior

 `#[sea_orm(belongs_to ...)]` generated with FK defined, 

### Reproduces How Often

 Always

### Workarounds

 None

## Versions

```
$ sea-orm-cli --version
sea-orm-cli 2.0.0-rc.28
```

`sea-orm-cli generate entity` panics with `"not implemented"` on `Decimal` column (2.0.0-rc.41)

## Description

`sea-orm-cli generate entity` panics with `"not implemented"` when processing a `Decimal` column using the `--entity-format expanded` option.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the following command (using a Neon Postgres database), replace database url with actual database url:

```bash
sea-orm-cli generate entity \
  -o database/entity/src/ \
  -u "postgresql://..." \
  --entity-format expanded \
  --max-connections 1
```

2. The command processes several tables successfully, then fails on the `exercises` table.

## Expected Behavior

The CLI should successfully generate entity files for all tables, including those with `Decimal` columns.

## Actual Behavior

Generation fails with a panic:

```
thread 'main' (368462) panicked at /home/.../sea-orm-codegen-2.0.0-rc.41/src/entity/column.rs:209:22:
not implemented
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
Aborted (core dumped)
```

It fails specifically while processing this column in the `exercises` table:
- `pass_mark`: `Option<Decimal>`

## Reproduces How Often

Always (on this schema).

## Workarounds

- Use `--entity-format dense` instead of `expanded` (recommended for SeaORM 2.0 anyway).
- Manually write entities using the new `#[sea_orm::model]` macro.

## Versions

- `sea-orm-cli`: `2.0.0-rc.41`
- `sea-orm-codegen`: `2.0.0-rc.41`
- Database: **PostgreSQL** (Neon serverless)
- OS: Linux

[bug] tauri.conf.json5 changes not applied in `tauri dev` watch mode

### Describe the bug

Came up in https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri-docs/pull/776#issuecomment-1213351875 / https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri-docs/pull/776#issuecomment-1213486568

While you're in tauri dev mode, changes to the config file won't get applied unless you manually rerun tauri dev, even though the file watcher correctly triggers a rebuild.

For example, changing the allowlist doesn't update the feature flag in Cargo.toml without a manual restart.

To be clear, it does try to rebuild automatically, but you get an issue about incorrect feature flags.

So far i only tested it with json**5** and the allowlist and package.name

Oh also there seems to be an issue that it _always_ runs the build script even if there were no relevant changes as far as i understand it.

### Reproduction

1. Enable the config-json5 feature. Doesn't matter if only on tauri or tauri and tauri-build
2. disable the allowlist
3. run tauri dev
4. enable something on the allowlist. Changing the app name works too to get an error.
5. the watcher will trigger a new build, but won't apply the changes, It will complain about mismatched feature flags, check Cargo.toml and confirm that they are wrong/missing.

_No response_

## Bug Report

### Version

`axum 0.8.0-rc.1`

### Platform

`Linux cemoktra 6.8.0-50-generic #51-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat Nov  9 17:58:29 UTC 2024 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux`

### Crates

`axum`

### Description

Previously the `Path` extractor returned 400 in case serde serialization failed. Now it returns 500. In the following example `abc` is no a valid uuid, so it should result in 400,but it actually ends in 500

```
let test = Router::new().route("/{arg}/static", get(|_extractor: Path<Uuid>| async move {}));

let response = app
    .oneshot(Request::get("/abc/static").body(Body::empty()).unwrap())
    .await
    .unwrap();

assert_eq!(response.status(), StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
```

Feature: BSON support for compact binary serialization

- [x] I have looked for existing issues (including closed) about this

## Feature Request
Add a BSON version of JSON serialization/deserialization support
https://docs.rs/bson/2.15.0/bson/

### Motivation
I need to reduce network traffic in my application by compressing the JSON data being sent and received. BSON's binary format is significantly more compact than JSON for most data structures, which would help reduce bandwidth usage and improve response times.

JSON's text format includes a lot of redundant characters and doesn't encode numbers efficiently. BSON stores data in a binary format that's both smaller and faster to parse. This would be especially beneficial for applications sending large amounts of data or operating in bandwidth-constrained environments.

Right now, I'm stuck with verbose JSON payloads that take up unnecessary bandwidth. Having native BSON support would let me easily switch to a more efficient format without major code changes.

### Proposal
Add BSON support similar to how JSON is currently handled. The implementation should use the existing `bson` crate and be behind an optional feature flag so it doesn't bloat the core library.

The API should feel consistent with the current JSON implementation while taking advantage of BSON's unique features. Error handling should integrate cleanly with the existing error types, and we'd need good documentation with examples showing common use cases.

### Alternatives
I considered just doing the Axum-to-BSON conversion manually in my application code, but it would become a hindrance to maintain when I change between lib versions.

Handling of HEAD requests violates RFC 9110

## Bug Report

Axum responds to HEAD requests with `content-length: 0`, which (in almost all cases) violates HTTP semantics. Refer to [RFC 9110, Sec. 9.3.2, Paragraph 2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#section-9.3.2-2).

If the value for the `content-length` header that would be produced in response to a GET request is not known at the time of responding to a HEAD request, then it should be omitted, not included with a value of 0.

Real-world example: A handler that archives data into a `*.zip` file and responds with the archive. Assume that there is quite a lot of data, so archiving just to know the length of the hypothetical response to GET would be considered wasteful. It would be incorrect to respond with `content-length: 0`, because the archive itself will likely not be the empty file.

The same argument is used in https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum/pull/755#issuecomment-1037931480, so I allow myself to mention the author: @davidpdrsn

Previous issues that seem to be related:
 - https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum/issues/730
 - https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum/issues/747

### Version

Checked out https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum.git at commit `9f4d52e310a6053e49f3db09ce02f723a7a3f5bb` which is `main` as of 2026-05-01.

### Platform

NixOS on Windows Subsystem for Linux, likely irrelevant.

```
Linux wsl 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Jun  5 18:30:46 UTC 2025 x86_64 GNU/Linux
```

### Description

I tried this code: https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum/blob/9f4d52e310a6053e49f3db09ce02f723a7a3f5bb/examples/handle-head-request/src/main.rs

Actual:

```shell-session
$ git clone https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum.git
$ cd axum/example/handle-head-request
$ cargo run -p example-handle-head-request
[build output]
listening on 127.0.0.1:3000
$ curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:3000/get-head
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
x-some-header: header from GET
content-length: 13
date: [current date and time]
$ curl -s -D - -o /dev/null --head http://127.0.0.1:3000/get-head
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-some-header: header from HEAD
content-length: 0
date: [current date and time]
```

Expected:

```diff
 $ git clone https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum.git
 $ cd axum/example/handle-head-request
 $ cargo run -p example-handle-head-request
 [build output]
 listening on 127.0.0.1:3000
 $ curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:3000/get-head
 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
 content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
 x-some-header: header from GET
 content-length: 13
 date: [current date and time]
 $ curl -s -D - -o /dev/null --head http://127.0.0.1:3000/get-head
 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
 x-some-header: header from HEAD
-content-length: 0
 date: [current date and time]
```

Alternative Resolution (more complicated to implement):

```diff

 $ cd axum/example/handle-head-request
 $ cargo run -p example-handle-head-request
 [build output]

 $ curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:3000/get-head
 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
 content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
 x-some-header: header from GET
 content-length: 13
 date: [current date and time]
 $ curl -s -D - -o /dev/null --head http://127.0.0.1:3000/get-head

Handling of HEAD requests violates RFC 9110

## Bug Report

Axum responds to HEAD requests with `content-length: 0`, which (in almost all cases) violates HTTP semantics. Refer to [RFC 9110, Sec. 9.3.2, Paragraph 2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#section-9.3.2-2).

If the value for the `content-length` header that would be produced in response to a GET request is not known at the time of responding to a HEAD request, then it should be omitted, not included with a value of 0.

Real-world example: A handler that archives data into a `*.zip` file and responds with the archive. Assume that there is quite a lot of data, so archiving just to know the length of the hypothetical response to GET would be considered wasteful. Correcting one or the other should be done, I'd prefer going towards expr since that allows using the std::concat! macro to build queries.

(
Allowing for !concat would be more standard than the custom allowance for '+' to add together strings, but maybe there is some problem with that that I don't know about?
)

raw_text:
Sqlite Pool does not need split

### Good news:

You might not need a split of readers and writers for SQLite as proposed in #459.

If you do that, you will hinder the life of developer greatly and there is a better way.

There are two errors people run into often with SQLite:

* `SQLITE_BUSY`
* `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT` (especially in WAL mode)

And both of them can be **easily avoided** without the split.

`SQLITE_BUSY` can be avoided by:

* using `busy_timeout`
* resetting prepared statement after use

`SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT` happens when transaction starts in `DEFERRED` mode with simple `BEGIN` - becomes "reader" - and later tries to upgrade to "writer" while another thread already became "writer" but waits until "reader" finish.

And SQLite will detect this deadlock and will cause the first thread to error out. This is explained in detail by [SQLite Isolation] article.

Often the solution is to use `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for such transactions to become "writer" from the beginning.

If you choose this path, you are free from locking problems.

### Bad news:

SQLite support in SQLx has fundamental things to fix, unfortunately.

* prepared statements are not reset after use
* the use of `SqliteRow` is not constrained by any lifetime leading to #634

On the other hand, Diesel is doing things just right. Every prepared statement is reset just after the use ends and the lifetime of the row is constrained.
Refer to [`StatementUse`] struct.

I prepared two Gists to show the problem:

* [Diesel Gist]
* [SQLx Gist]

Diesel runs fine while SQLx struggles.

I prepared two pull-requests to make the situation better (but still not ideal).

* a fix for `fetch_optional` in [PR852] (this PR also fixes #662).
* a support for `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` in [PR851]

I have also added support for `synchronous` setting in [PR850] (it is common to set it to `NORMAL` with `WAL` which greatly improves performance).

PS: My personal opinion is that many would benefit from proper guidance on common defaults (`journal_mode=WAL` + `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` + `synchronous=NORMAL`). It is not understood widely, especially for people new to SQLite.

[SQLite Isolation]: https://sqlite.org/isolation.html
[Diesel Gist]: https://gist.github.com/markazmierczak/6ffad42239d9fe7d3bd6e9f0d698eeb9
[SQLx Gist]: https://gist.github.com/markazmierczak/f408ac8f5b4f3ca37bfdd5cc22fc3fe4
[`StatementUse`]: https://github.com/diesel-rs/diesel/blob/8d3c955b244351aa5ec1af34d2c91b669d25269c/diesel/src/sqlite/connection/stmt.rs
[PR850]: https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/pull/850
[PR851]: https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/pull/851
[PR852]: https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/pull/852

Sqlx field attributes difference between query_as<_, type> and query_as!

### Bug Description
While trying to map a SQL response to a custom struct using sqlx I noticed some weird behaviour between query_as<_, type> and query_as!

**My structs are the following:**
```
  #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Debug, sqlx::FromRow)]
  pub struct SaveSimulation {
    name: Option<String>,

    // #[serde(rename = "valid")]
    // #[sqlx(default)]
    // valid: bool,

    #[serde(rename = "routes")]
    routes: Option<Vec<Routing>>,
  }

  #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Debug, sqlx::Type, sqlx::FromRow)]
  struct Routing {
    #[serde(rename = "id")]
    route_id: i64,

    #[serde(rename = "name")]
    name: Option<String>,
  }
```

With these structs I tried to query data from the database. Which only works when field with `#[sqlx(default)]` isn't used.This query does work and gives me the desired data from the database but doesn't let me use the `#[sqlx(default)]`:
```
  let simulations = sqlx::query_as!(SaveSimulation,
    r#"
    SELECT S.name,
      ARRAY_AGG((R.route_id, R.name)) as "routes: Vec<Routing>"
    FROM simulations S
      JOIN routes R ON R.simulation_uid = S.simulation_uid
    GROUP BY S.simulation_uid
    "#
  )
  .fetch_one(&pool) // -> Vec<Country>
  .await?;
```


**Now I enable the valid field in the structs:**
```
  #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Debug, sqlx::FromRow)]
  pub struct SaveSimulation {
    name: Option<String>,

    #[serde(rename = "valid")]
    #[sqlx(default)]
    valid: bool,

    #[serde(rename = "routes")]
    routes: Option<Vec<Routing>>,
  }

  #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Debug, sqlx::Type, sqlx::FromRow)]
  struct Routing {
    #[serde(rename = "id")]
    route_id: i64,

    #[serde(rename = "name")]
    name: Option<String>,
  }
```

**The same query now doesn't work anymore:**
```
error[E0063]: missing field `valid` in initializer of `SaveSimulation`
   --> src\main.rs:494:37
    |
494 |   let simulations = sqlx::query_as!(SaveSimulation,
    |                                     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ missing `valid`
```

When I now switch to the usage of `query_as::<_, SaveSimulation>` instead of `query_as!` using the default field now works but I can't use the vec<> field anymore:
```
  let simulations = sqlx::query_as::<_, SaveSimulation>(
    r#"
      SELECT S.name      
      FROM simulations S
      GROUP BY S.simulation_uid
    "#,
  )
  .fetch_one(&pool).await?;
```

Now I tried to use vec<> again:
```
  let simulations = sqlx::query_as::<_, SaveSimulation>(
    r#"
      SELECT S.name,
        ARRAY_AGG((R.route_id, R.name)) as "routes: Vec<Routing>"
      FROM simulations S
        JOIN routes R ON R.simulation_uid = S.simulation_uid
      GROUP BY S.simulation_uid
    "#,
  )
  .fetch_one(&pool).await?;
```

**When I try to use vec<> I get the following error:**
```
error[E0599]: the method `fetch_one` exists for struct `QueryAs<'_, _, SaveSimulation, _>`, but its trait bounds were not satisfied
   --> src\main.rs:490:4
    |
368 |     pub struct SaveSimulation {
    |     ------------------------- doesn't satisfy `SaveSimulation: FromRow<'r, _>`
...
481 |     let simulations = sqlx::query_as::<_, SaveSimulation>(
    |  _____________________-
482 | |     r#"
483 | |       SELECT S.name,
484 | |         ARRAY_AGG((R.route_id, R.name)) as "routes: Vec<Routing>"
...   |
489 | |   )
490 | |   .fetch_one(&pool).await?;
    | |   -^^^^^^^^^ method cannot be called on `QueryAs<'_, _, SaveSimulation, _>` due to unsatisfied trait bounds
    | |___|
```


Does anyone knows why the sqlx field attributed only work with the `QueryAs<'_, _, SaveSimulation, _>` approach? And how to use this combined with the vec<> usage?

### Info
* SQLx version: 0.7
* SQLx features enabled: [ "runtime-tokio", "tls-native-tls" ]
* Database server and version: Postgres 11
* Operating system: Windows 11
* `rustc --version`: rustc --version

raw_text:
Allow --target-version to revert migrations with `-f`/`--force` flag

### I have found these related issues/pull requests

Relates to #2538

### Description

`sqlx migrate run --target-version [version]` is only allowed to apply `up` migrations, and will give an error if the target version is older than the latest applied migration. Likewise, `revert` is only allowed to apply `down` migrations; there is no command that migrates to a specific version regardless of the current version of the database.

I'm working on a Helm chart that deploys an application that requires a database. An init container first fetches the complete list of migrations, and runs those migrations up to the required version with a superuser account, after which the application itself can run with fewer privileges. This works great, but Helm charts can also be rolled back to previous versions, and while this isn't super common, doing so will likely break the application if the database isn't rolled back properly as well. I cannot expect users to revert the migrations manually, but I do want to support rollbacks, so it would be useful if the init container could revert migrations as well.

### Prefered solution

A `-f`/`--force` flag that allows `sqlx migrate run --target-version [version]` to apply `down` migrations if necessary.

In the meantime, I can apply both `sqlx migrate run --target-version [version]` and `sqlx migrate revert --target-version [version]`, knowing that one of them will return an error.

### Is this a breaking change? Why or why not?

The new functionality only applies when using a previously non-existent flag, and supplying non-existent flags to the CLI will currently throw an error, so it's not a breaking change.
